News.title: Man, 44, charged with murder after beloved mum, 44, found dead in flat above city pub
News.content:
MURDER CHARGE Man, 44, charged with murder after beloved mum, 44, found dead in flat above city pub







Next

A MAN has been charged with murder after a beloved mum was found dead in a flat above a city pub.

Leanne Park, 44, was pronounced dead in the flat over The Greyhound on Parkgate, Darlington, at about 9.15pm on September 23.



Andrew Bell, of Darlington, has been charged with murder and remanded in police custody, Durham Police said.

Bell, 44, will appear at Newton Aycliffe Magistrates’ Court on Monday.



A 27-year-old man arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender has been released on bail, the force added.

Ms Park’s family paid tribute to her as “the best mam, nana, daughter, and friend we could wish for”.



In a statement yesterday, they said: “She was loved by everyone and would do anything for anyone.

“She was the life and soul of the party and loved to dance.



“We love her so much and miss her more than words can describe. We are completely devastated. Her death has ripped the heart out of our family.

“We are grateful for all the kind messages and the support since her death.

“We ask that everyone remembers her for the kind-hearted woman she was.”

Emergency services had been called to the pub at around 9.15pm on Wednesday, September 23.

Tragically, despite the best efforts of medics, Leanne was pronounced dead at the scene.



Durham Police said their investigation remains ongoing as specialist crime scene investigators continue to work at the scene.

A cordon will remain in place for some time, they added.

Leanne’s death has sparked an outpouring of tributes, including with bouquets of flowers which have been left outside the pub.

One tribute read: “Always in our hearts, taken too soon. Heaven has gained a beautiful angel”.

Another said: “RIP our beautiful Auntie. You are so loved and going to be a huge miss, love you always”.



Her colleagues at the Ventress Hall care home in Darlington previously said she would “do anything for anybody”.

News.title: Body pulled from water in search for missing teen who vanished 10 days ago sparking urgent seaside search
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TRAGIC GEORGE Body pulled from water in search for missing teen who vanished 10 days ago sparking urgent seaside search







Next

A BODY has been found in the agonising search for an 18-year-old who vanished in a seaside town ten days ago.

George, from Portishead in Somerset, was last seen in the coastal town at around 8.20pm on Thursday, September 17.



A large search was launched in the days that followed, involving cops, coastguard teams, the RNLI and other emergency services.

But police have now confirmed a body has been recovered from a coastal location near Newport on Sunday morning.



Avon and Somerset Police said the clothing worn by the man matched what George had been wearing when he was last seen.

A formal identification process will now be carried out.



Cops have informed George’s family of the latest development.

The force says they are continuing to support them with a specially trained officer.

The force added that the death is not being treated as suspicious.

It will now be a matter for the coroner.



George’s disappearance had prompted repeated appeals for information as emergency crews search the coastline.

Neighbourhood chief inspector Andy Barry previously praised the “strength and resilience” of George’s family during the search.

He said: “I would like to recognise the strength and resilience of George’s family during this time and we continue to keep them updated through a specialist liaison officer.”

The force added that George’s family had been touched by the support they have received.

News.title: Burnham’s free social care for all plan is classic spend-now, worry-later politics from our “good vibes” PM
News.content:
THE SUN SAYS Burnham’s free social care for all plan is classic spend-now, worry-later politics from our “good vibes” PM

Carefree PM







Next

ANDY Burnham yesterday opened Labour’s conference with another grand promise.

This time he vowed to provide free social care for all, yet left out one tiny detail: who is going to foot the bill, estimated at £18.5billion?

We can hazard a pretty good guess that it will mean another raid on the pay packets or savings of millions of hard-working families already being squeezed from every direction.



It’s classic spend-now, worry-later politics from our “good vibes” PM



In typical fashion, he grabbed the conference platform glory for himself and gave Whitehall troubleshooter Louise Casey the nightmare job of balancing the books.

Burnham says he wants a system where “everyone contributes”, either through more income tax or a ten per cent death tax on all estates.

“Nothing’s off the table,” he declared.

But you can bet he won’t ask the ten million people on working-age benefits to cough up a single penny to help deliver his promise.

He should remember when Theresa May devised a social-care plan dubbed the “dementia tax” in 2017.

The Tories lost their overall majority and the idea was dropped.

Burnham beware. Fed-up taxpayers have a simple but effective way of saying enough is enough.



Growing terror

THE plot to bomb RAF Fairford bears all the hallmarks of the outlawed Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

The Iranian terror group — banned by the Home Secretary in July — declared the Gloucestershire base a target after it was used by US warplanes to mount defensive air strikes on Iran.

It is chilling to think an attack on a military garrison on the British mainland was averted only because of a hero farmer’s quick thinking.

Two important questions need answering: Why did it take so long to ban the IRGC?

And how much longer must we wait for the Government to beef up our hollowed-out defences?



Bingo bungle

LABOUR is planning to tax our fun and working folk will end up paying the price.

If the Chancellor hikes gambling taxes on fruit machines next month, hundreds of bingo hall workers face the sack.

Andy Burnham says he puts all his ideas to the “Makerfield test” — asking how they would impact areas like his own constituency.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Pollsters have done that job for him and found that more than half of people on his home turf think betting outlets are at the heart of community life.

It’s time to stop sticking your nose in our business, protect community jobs, and let people enjoy a good night out.

News.title: How farmer heroically foiled RAF base ‘bomb plot’ after seeing ‘something pretty serious’ as she drove home from party
News.content:
Next

A HERO farmer thwarted a massive terror attack on an RAF base after spotting suspects in balaclavas on her way home from a party.

The late-night sighting metres from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire led to the arrest of five men and seizure of three vans full of explosives.



The plot came two months after Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said the base — used to launch US bomber strikes on the terror regime — was a “legitimate target”.

If the attack proves to be state-sponsored it would be one of the biggest by a foreign nation on British soil since WW2.



Prime Minister Andy Burnham called the incident “deeply concerning” and promised the Government will “always take every step necessary” to protect people.

A sharp-eyed farmer was hailed a hero last night after she foiled a bomb attack on the RAF base.

The sharp-eyed farmer spotted men in balaclavas running close to the base as she drove home from a bash with her husband early yesterday.

The mum told how three vans were blocking the road outside the village of Whelford, Gloucs, adding: “We had to turn around and drive away.

“When we did that, we saw a group of men with masks and balaclavas running in front of us.”

The woman tried to call the base, used to launch US strikes on Iran, but could not get through so dialled 999.



She also left a message on her local WhatsApp group urging villagers to lock doors.

Armed cops swooped on the five suspects as they headed towards the base, seizing chemicals and incendiary devices from the vans, one of which had a fake sign.

The suspects, of Middle Eastern appearance, were pictured shirtless and handcuffed by the roadside.



A major incident was declared, 85 homes were evacuated and residents were taken to a leisure centre while experts made the bombs safe.

It was suspected bombs were going to be used to attack nearby RAF Fairford, which Iran named a “legitimate target” in July.

US President Donald Trump claimed an investigation into the plot was underway before the arrests.

He said: “Working with Britain, it was an amazing job.

“We had them under investigation.



“They were looking to do big damage to our fort, and working with the British worked out great.

“It may have been Scotland Yard, I don’t know.

“We worked with a lot of them.



“We had them under view for a long time and we got them.”

Efforts have been doubled into tracing Iran’s Revolutionary Guard cells feared to be operating in Britain since the July threat.

And locals said that security has been reinforced at the base in recent weeks.

However, it was understood that yesterday’s arrests did not follow any specific information.

The farmer, in her 50s, said of the suspects: “They were running from where the vans were.



“Some were hiding from us.

“They were all in hoods and balaclavas and masks.

“They were hiding in the hedge and the field.

“I just thought what the hell are they doing.

“Some ran into the fields, and some turned to run towards the air base.



“We realised this was something pretty serious.

“We drove away.

“They ran one way and we drove the other.”

The woman, who has lived in the village for 25 years, told The Sun: “I think they were running from us because our vehicle happens to be quite similar to the vehicles that the base police use.

“We’ve been told we probably did avert whatever it was they were doing, so it’s very lucky.”



The woman added: “I haven’t heard any more from the base police.

“They don’t have an answerphone so you can’t leave a message so I don’t even know if they know I tried to phone them.

“I’m pretty horrified it was me who had to phone them and they didn’t know themselves.

“It was terrifying, horrific.

“When you look back on it and realise you were so close to the guys who had been arrested.”



She added of the base: “They had credible threats, they locked down the base but still this happened.

“If we hadn’t seen them it could have been terrible.”

The woman also said that she believed she spotted more than the five men arrested.

She said: “The worst thing is that we saw more than five people and they keep saying they arrested five.

“They had the helicopters searching.”



Prime suspect Iran has form for rent-a-thugs By JEROME STARKEY, Defence Editor IRAN is the prime suspect for three disturbing reasons. Firstly, Tehran called Fairford a “legitimate target” after it was used to launch strikes in July. Secondly, we have known for years that Tehran hires rent-a-thugs because it is cheaper and easier than deploying its Revolutionary Guard Corps. Thirdly, Iran has form. MI5 chief Ken McCallum revealed his spies disrupted 20 “potentially lethal” Iran-backed plots last year. Russian attacks are also soaring. Germany has blamed explosive drones found at Leipzig airport on Kremlin spies. But Moscow has less to gain than Iran from targeting a US airbase. The picture should become clearer when the Fairford suspects are interviewed and vehicles are examined.

Gloucestershire Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone said: “At around 12:45am today police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles travelling towards RAF Fairford.

Armed police officers responded and arrested five men in the Whelford area on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act.

“The men were taken into custody. A 400-metre cordon has been put in place around the vehicles while the Army’s explosives, ordinance and disposal unit examine them.

“As a precaution around 85 households were advised to evacuate the area.”

He added: “The emergency services have well-rehearsed plans for dealing with major incidents.



“A cordon is in place as a precaution and the public can expect to see an emergency services presence in the area for some time.

“A nearby leisure centre has been opened to provide a safe space for anyone evacuated and unable to go to friends or relatives.”

The five suspects were later further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act.

Police had not said where they are being held.

Counter Terrorism Policing’s Vicki Evans said: “We are in the early stages of an investigation, and five men remain in custody.”



Locals reported armed guards and tractors had been placed at the entrance to RAF Fairford in the last few weeks.

Residents told how a helicopter hovered over the village at 1.30am yesterday before police turfed them out of homes.

One woman said: “We were asleep and they were just banging on our door.

“They said it was a critical incident and we’ve got to leave straight away, and they basically wouldn’t leave the doorstep until we left.

“We just had to throw our clothes on and come.



“We didn’t know anything.

“The police literally waited at the door.

“I didn’t even brush my teeth.

“We didn’t know what, but we knew it must be serious.”

The residents in 85 homes were unable to return last night as a police cordon remained in place.



Chris Phillips, former head of the National Counter Terrorism Security Office, paid tribute to the woman who spotted the suspects, saying: “She’s a hero and deserves a medal as she has saved a lot of lives.

“Clearly on this occasion the police and security services were not specifically aware of what was happening.

“It was very lucky that the suspects were spotted by this lady.”

Mr Phillips said Iran was the most likely suspect for the attack, with jihadi extremists and Russia being less likely perpetrators.

He added: “This may well be an IRGC sleeper cell in this country that has been woken up to do something.”



Mr Phillips said it was vital to find the bomb factory where the devices and chemicals had been stored to see if more remain.

Britain gave the US authority to use RAF Fairford for B-1 bombers to attack Iranian missile sites which have been targeting ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran identified RAF Fairford as a legitimate target in its July statement, prompting a response from Britain that it “stands ready 24/7 to defend itself.”

Around 20 attacks by Iran on the UK have been foiled in recent years, according to the security services.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage yesterday urged authorities to identify the RAF Fairford suspects.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “I’ve been warning both in and out of Parliament for many months about Iranian agents coming into to UK via small boats across the Channel.

“We deserve to be told the truth about the Fairford bomb plotters identities.”

News.title: Rookie cop ‘stabbed in neck’ while responding to call chased ‘knifeman’ covered in blood before being rushed to hospital
News.content:
Next

A ROOKIE cop has been hailed a hero after stopping an armed suspect who allegedly stabbed him in the neck as he tried to flee.

Constable Wesley Thomas, a married father of two young children, had only been a police officer for 10 weeks when he heroically Tasered the alleged knifeman in Brisbane.



Josey Collins, 35, has since been charged with two counts of attempted murder.

Thomas and a senior constable, 52, had responded to reports of a domestic disturbance at a house on Bogong Street, Hemmant at around 5.10am on Sunday.



Collins had allegedly injured his father before turning the knife on the graduate copper.

When officers were unable to de-escalate the conflict, Collins allegedly slashed the senior constable’s arm before stabbing Thomas in the neck and torso.

An injured Thomas bravely chased the assailant and used a Taser on him, despite blood pouring out of his neck.

He was given first aid at the scene, before being rushed to Princess Alexandra Hospital in a “potentially life-threatening condition”.

Chief Superintendent Heath McQueen said it was a “very traumatic incident for our officers to attend”.

Queensland Police Union president Shane Prior praised both officers and called Thomas “an absolute hero” for his actions, before confirming he underwent surgery for his injuries.



He said: “Don’t be mistaken, this situation could have very easily resulted in the death of the police officer today.

“We may very well have been talking about a scenario where an officer was killed today just doing their job.”

According to reports, Thomas remains in hospital in a stable condition, as well as being awake and speaking on Sunday night.

Prior added that the constable had only graduated the police academy in July.

McQueen commended the “commitment and courage” of the officers and the “split second decisions” they made in a dangerous situation.



He said: “This incident highlights the inherent risk that our officers face on a daily basis in serving the community.”

He added that Thomas would undergo further surgery for his injuries.

Collins allegedly took off and stole a bike before he was arrested around 7am about three kilometres away in Manly West.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A friendly neighbour, Ricky Skott, handed key evidence to police – a knife he found in a nearby alleyway.

Collins will appear in Cleveland Magistrates Court on Monday.

News.title: Afghan small boat migrant ‘smuggled girl, 14, into the UK after kidnapping and sexually assaulting her’
News.content:
BORDER FARCE Afghan small boat migrant ‘smuggled girl, 14, into the UK after kidnapping and sexually assaulting her’







Next

A DINGHY migrant smuggled a girl of 14 into ­Britain after kidnapping and sexually assaulting her, a court has heard.

It is believed to be the first case in which an abducted child has been brought across the Channel in a small boat.



The Afghan national is said to have lured her away from a camp in Belgium in June 2025.

After allegedly sexually assaulting the teen, he is then said to have brought her across France and sneaked her into the UK.



The man, who can’t be named as it could identify his alleged victim, was found living with the girl in Manchester.

He was arrested in West London last month.



The man has given three birth dates, and could be 27, 21 or 18.

He has agreed to be extradited to Belgium to face trial this year.

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “This case is truly sickening.

“This vile individual should have never been allowed to come to the UK in the first place.”



The Home Office said it could not comment on individual cases.

Westminster magistrates’ court heard the girl, from Turkey, had been at a reception centre for applicants for international protection.

Residents are free to enter and leave during the day while their asylum requests are being evaluated.

Belgian police say the man was seen leaving the camp with the girl.

Cops put out an appeal to find her shortly after she disappeared.



The National Crime Agency said: “A man wanted by authorities in Belgium was arrested by officers from the NCA’s National Extradition Unit on August 19 in Feltham, West London.

“He remains in custody as extradition proceedings continue”.

News.title: Fury as cost of interpreters and translators used in UK courts soars to £40million in just one year – and YOU pay for it
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

LOST IN TRANSLATION Fury as cost of interpreters and translators used in UK courts soars to £40million in just one year – and YOU pay for it







Next

TAXPAYERS forked out more than £40million on interpreters and translators for the justice system last year, data shows.

The sum — which equates to £800,000 per week — is thought to be a record for a single year across courts in England and Wales.

Spoken language interpreters made up the bulk of the bill at £30.1million.

Tory MP Sir John Hayes obtained the figures through a parliamentary question.





He told The Sun: “There has to be an expectation that people are speaking English, or at least learning it.

“Taxpayers are being ripped off.

“There’s now an entire industry of court translations because it is so lucrative.

“This is a serious problem and it has a massive knock on effect on court backlogs too.”

A Ministry of Justice spokeswoman said: “These services ensure justice is fair.

“Without them, cases risk being dragged through costly appeals, driving up the bill for the taxpayer.

“We’re also funding record levels of court sitting days to get the backlog down.”

News.title: Gobsmacked job hunters applying for litter picking role told they need FOUR YEARS experience in ‘bonkers’ advert
News.content:
Next

JOB hunters applying for a litter-picking role were told they cannot pick it up as they go along — as the employer demanded four years’ experience.

Gobsmacked applicants were told they needed a host of other skills too.

The advert stated three years of “grounds maintenance” expertise was “preferred”.

It also said the right person for the position should have “landscaping/gardening experience”, the “ability to communicate effectively” and “strong customer service skills when interacting with the public”.





Grounds maintenance firm Peter Ashley Ltd said in the ad, on jobseeker website Indeed: “We are currently seeking a dedicated Mobile Litter Picker to join our team in maintaining cleanliness in public spaces who has the ability to work alone with a can-do attitude.”

One job hunter blasted it as “bonkers” after realising he did not have the required skills.

The man, who did not want to be named, said: “When I saw the advert say litter picking, I thought, ‘I could do that,’ and I went to apply.

“Then I was left flabbergasted.



“I mean, what experience do you need to pick up litter? Landscape gardening?

“I only wanted to do it to earn a bit of cash on the side.”

The firm, in Wilmslow, Cheshire, said of the four years’ experience requirement for the three-day week role: “It should say preferred rather than required.

“It’s a clerical error.



“This has since been corrected.”

News.title: Heidi Alexander says 'enough is enough' as she confirms Avanti West Coast services to be nationalised
News.content:
Heidi Alexander says 'enough is enough' as she confirms Avanti West Coast services to be nationalised

Heidi Alexander vowed Burnham's Labour is committed to 'putting essential services back in public hands, connecting people to opportunity and delivering growth in every postcode'

View 4 Images Heidi Alexander's announcement will have been welcomed by Brit commuters (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

Avanti West Coast services will be nationalised from March next year, the Transport Secretary has announced.

‌



Heidi Alexander said “enough is enough” as she vowed to end poor service for rail passengers using the train service. The Government on Sunday announced it will take control of Avanti West Coast’s services from March 7, as part of a wider drive to put essential services back in public control.

‌



Avanti West Coast passengers have been experiencing frequent disruption on one of the country's busiest routes for years.

‌



Tech firms could earn social media ban exemption if they make their platforms safe READ MORE :

View 4 Images Heidi Alexander has said Avanti West Coast services will be nationalised from next year (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Performance remains behind the industry average with passengers frequently frustrated by delays and cancellations. Infrastructure issues along the West Coast Main Line resulting from long-term underinvestment are the biggest cause of disruption for passengers, ministers said.

Ms Alexander said: "For years, we've heard stories of Avanti underperforming, with passengers left paying the price. Enough is enough.

‌



"That is why we will bring Avanti into public ownership at the earliest opportunity, in March next year. This Labour government is committed to putting essential services back in public hands, connecting people to opportunity and delivering growth in every postcode – and this move reflects that commitment."

View 4 Images Alexander said the Government would make the move after years of Avanti underperforming (Image: Getty Images)

“We will also introduce a comprehensive improvement plan, focused on delivering for passengers, not shareholders.” The government is on track to complete all public ownership transfers by the end of 2027 ahead of setting up Great British Railways.

‌



The news comes after the Culture Secretary suggested tech firms could earn an exemption to an incoming UK social media ban if they make their platforms safe for under 16s.

In a panel at Labour conference, Lisa Nandy said social media giants could get themselves removed from a list of banned platforms if they tackle unsafe features. The Cabinet minister said ministers will draw up a list of existing applications that will face restrictions but that they would also look at "safety by design" and a "safety by feature-led approach".

View 4 Images The Government said Avanti West Coast would be nationalised by next year (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

“We’re going to do proper, comprehensive legislation so that it doesn't just incorporate the specific apps, it incorporates the features that we believe are not safe," Ms Nandy told the event, which was hosted by the Molly Rose Foundation (MRF).

"So there will be a way for companies, if they want to innovate and they want to change, to be able to get themselves essentially off that list. But that's up to them.

"We believe that's their choice. They can decide to innovate if they want to, and we believe they should because we think they have their social and moral obligations. But whether they do it or not, the government has an obligation here and we intend to act.”

News.title: Labour conference: Lisa Nandy reveals 'real Ed Sheeran' she knows after star faced 'horrendous hate and bile'
News.content:
Lisa Nandy has spoken out about the "most horrendous hate and bile" directed at Ed Sheeran in recent weeks.

The Culture Secretary, speaking at a fringe event for The Mirror's Britain Talks project, praised the musician for his secret work bringing music to schools.

She said people must be able to disagree in a constructive way. Ms Nandy recalled getting a phone call from Sheeran, telling the event: "I'm going to start with something a bit controversial.

"I've spent the week answering questions about Ed Sheeran. He was somebody I got to know a couple of years ago when he rang up.

"And he said 'I've just read that you're the first entirely state-educated Cabinet in British history, and I'm so excited because I believe passionately that kids should have access to music in schools, can you help?'

"And we started on a piece of work. He has poured so much money into that, both in Ipswich and all over the country. He's never told anyone, he's never asked for praise, he's never asked for support.

"The first time I went to see what he was doing in Ipswich, he put on an impromptu gig for some of the kids from his old school. They didn't know it was him, they just knew it was a local act.

"I've never seen the magic on those children's faces, and some of the teachers told me later, it would change their lives."

She continued that she was shocked by the onslaught he has endured. Ms Nandy said: "He's someone who wears his politics lightly. He's not a politician, but he's somebody who believes that doing the right thing matters.

"He's got involved with a few causes over the years; he's got a friend who is very pro-Palestine, as am I, and he's used that platform for good to talk up to people about what is happening in Palestine.

"And when his promoters decided that they didn't want to continue with that concert, Ed Sheeran found himself in a position of the most horrendous hate and bile that I've seen.

"And you know, I'm a politician, I've been at this 17 years, I see a lot of it. I only have to look on X to see it, even while I'm talking here, a lot of it will be directed at me, and (fellow panelists) Tracy (Brabin) and Ros (Wynne Jones), and others.

"But honestly, I don't know how we came to a place where not only can we not disagree agreeably, but where you're not even allowed to wear your politics lightly."

News.title: A body has been found after an 18-year-old went missing 10 days ago
News.content:
A body has been found after an 18-year-old went missing 10 days ago

Avon and Somerset Police today said a body had been recovered in Wales on Sunday morning with items of clothing matching those of an 18-year-old who went missing on September 17 in north Somerset

View Image A body has been found in the search for an 18-year-old man named George (Image: Avon and Somerset Police)

The teenager, named as George, went missing from the seaside town of Portishead in north Somerset on September 17.

‌



Avon and Somerset Police today said a body had been recovered on Sunday morning from water at a coastal location near Newport in Wales.

‌



In the days following his disappearance, police, coastguard, RNLI and other services launched a huge search for George but today the force shared the tragic news that George’s family had been informed of the terrible discovery, Wales Online reports.

‌



An Avon and Somerset Police spokesperson said: "The items of clothing worn by the man matched those George had last been seen wearing in Portishead on Thursday, September 17.

"As a matter of routine, a formal identification process will need to be undertaken. However, we have informed George’s family of this latest development and are continuing to provide them with support through a specially trained officer.

‌



"The death is not being treating as suspicious and will be a matter for the coroner going forward.

"While George’s family have been touched by all the offers of support they have received recently, quite understandably they are requesting their privacy is respected at this time.

"Finally, we would like to thank everyone who called in with information and shared our appeals, as well as Gwent Police and the RNLI for their involvement today."

Article continues below

During the search last week, neighbourhood chief inspector Andy Barry said: "I would like to recognise the strength and resilience of George’s family during this time and we continue to keep them updated through a specialist liaison officer."

News.title: Andy Burnham urged to introduce universal free school meals and end scourge of hunger
News.content:
Andy Burnham urged to introduce universal free school meals and end scourge of hunger

EXCLUSIVE: A year-long Right to Food Commission - led by the Labour MP Ian Byrne - warns food insecurity 'is a national crisis that needs an immediate emergency response'

View 2 Images Andy Burnham told food insecurity is a 'national crisis that needs an immediate emergency response' (Image: Victoria Jones/Shutterstock)

Andy Burnham is being urged to end the scourge of hunger across Britain with a string of measures including universal free school meals.

‌



It comes as a year-long Right to Food Commission - led by the Labour MP Ian Byrne - warns food insecurity "is a national crisis that needs an immediate emergency response".

‌



Based on sobering conversations across the country, the Commission said the new Prime Minister should act urgently to improve the lives of millions.

‌



Mr Byrne said: "We have heard harrowing evidence about the effect food insecurity is having on children. It is distressing, heartbreaking and utterly avoidable. We have also had it confirmed that we have an income problem, not a food problem in this country."

Last year the government announced it would extend eligibility for free school meals to all children in families who receive Universal Credit, helping an estimated 500,000 more kids.

Andy Burnham vows to fight next election with NHS-style social care plan READ MORE :

Angela Rayner insists no Cabinet split over migration reforms - despite criticism READ MORE :

View 2 Images Labour MP Ian Byrne warns food insecurity 'is a national crisis that needs an immediate emergency response' (Image: Andrew Teebay Liverpool Echo)

‌



But recommendations from the Commission - seen by The Mirror - urges the government to go further and make free school meals universal for all children up to the age of 18. They say this will "end school food debt and related stigma".

It demands an end to the five-week wait for Universal Credit after a claim is first made to avoid claimants facing an immediate "income and food crisis".

Among dozens of recommendations it also calls on ministers to establish a Cost of Living Unit based in the Prime Minister's office to alleviate pressures on families.

‌



And it urges the government to usher in a "Right to Food Bill" to combat food poverty.

It suggests reforms to capital gains tax and equalising it with income tax rates could raise more than enough to fund the £7.8billion needed to help vulnerable families.

One person told the Commission: "A right to food has to be a legal right, not a good intention. When something is a right, you can ask for it, question it, and expect it - instead of feeling it is your personal failing to go without.

‌



"That right has to have teeth: someone accountable for it, a way to challenge it when food is denied, and support that reaches people before they hit crisis, not after."

Another said: "Queuing at food banks is degrading, it adds to the stigma of not being able to provide decent food, clean clothes and a warm home. People who work feel embarrassed, stressed and often degraded just as must as stay at home families".

A third said: “Despite having two full time wages coming into my household, the rise in the cost of living has severely impacted our ability to afford healthy food for our family.”

‌



Chair of the Commission Barrie Margetts said: "The biggest example of the broken system Prime Minister Andy Burnham has rightly diagnosed is that in the sixth wealthiest country in the world we have 14 million people not knowing where their next meal is coming from.

"We have thousands of children going to school hungry and families having to choose between eating and heating, or eating and paying the rent.

"We know that child-ill health is linked to food insecurity - 700 children a year are hospitalised due to malnutrition, rickets or scurvy for goodness sake.

Article continues below

"A consistent message we heard across the country was the need for universal free school meals and holiday food provision for all school-aged children. This government must act now, put in place immediate relief measures and then work towards ending food insecurity once and for all by legislating to have a right to food.”

Vice-chair Mr Byrne added: "We have heard harrowing evidence about the effect food insecurity is having on children. It is distressing, heartbreaking and utterly avoidable."

Earlier this week polling from Amnesty International also found three-quarters (75%) of people have worried about the cost of food in the last year. The survey also found a massive majority - 82% - said there should be a legal right to food.

News.title: Nato countries preparing to evacuate in case of Russian attack
News.content:
Nato countries preparing to evacuate in case of Russian attack

Poland and Lithuania have been working on a framework for plans including evacuations in the event of an invasion by Russian forces

View 2 Images Polish border guards (file photo) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

NATO members are preparing plans for evacuating their populations in the event of an attack by Russia, according to reports.

‌



The plans focus around an area called the Suwałki Gap which connects the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad with the Russian-allied state of Belarus via a 60-mile stretch of the Polish and Lithuanian border.

‌



If Putin were to move his forces from Belarus across the gap to Kaliningrad, it would mean Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania could be cut off from the rest of Europe.

‌



Lithuania and Poland are currently working together on a framework for plans in case of Kremlin hostilities.

The Lithuanian National Crisis Management Centre has announced the creation of a bilateral agreement alongside nationwide drills in the country which included plans for evacuation along the Polish-Lithuanian border.

Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of Lithuania’s National Crisis Management Centre, explained plans will provide for the evacuation of Lithuania as well as Latvia and Estonia if necessary.

‌



View 2 Images The former border crossing between Poland and Lithuania (file photo) (Image: NurPhoto via Getty Images)

He said: “Procedures, logistics, and infrastructure capabilities are being analysed together with colleagues from Poland, and the plan itself should be developed once an agreement is reached between the two countries.”

Plans for a possible Russian invasion include border controls to “prevent people in certain key roles from leaving the country”.

‌



Some 3,000 officials and around 1,000 volunteers are taking part in the drills in Lithuania, along with around 20 Polish officials who have travelled there to take part.

Earlier this month Polish prime minister Donald Tusk warned Russia was preparing drone and missile strikes against countries that had been supporting Ukraine.

Donald Tusk issued the warning in the Polish parliament on last week, citing intelligence assessments which said Russia could carry out attacks against his country and other countries on NATO's eastern flank while presenting them as accidents.

‌



He said such attacks could be intended to test NATO's willingness to invoke Article 5, which requires member states to come to the aid of an ally under attack.

His words came just days before after Poland was forced to scramble fighter jets on Wednesday after a Russian military helicopter crossed into its airspace.

The Mi-8 made a brief incursion near the Polish town of Braniewo after entering the country’s airspace from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, the Polish military said.

Article continues below

NATO jets were again scrambled over the country last Saturday (September 19) after Russia launched a wave of jet-powered drone strikes across neighbouring Ukraine.

News.title: RAF Fairford: Everything you need to know about US-UK military base after 'terror plot' arrests
News.content:
RAF Fairford: Everything you need to know about US-UK military base after 'terror plot' arrests

The military base is the centrepiece of US-UK military cooperation, and has seen use over multiple conflicts since it was established to aid D-Day planning and deployment in 1944

View 7 Images Fairford is a primarily US base located in Gloucestershire (Image: Tom Wren / SWNS)

RAF Fairford and a small sleepy community in Gloucestershire were placed on lockdown this morning — as police swooped in to foil an alleged bomb plot at the shared US-UK military base.

Around 85 homes were evacuated an a 400-metre cordon placed around the village of Whelford, with Army bomb squads deployed to examine three vans after police received a call at around 12.45am today. Investigators said five men were arrested in the middle of the night at the air base on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. They were further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act.

The case is now in the hands of a joint team of US and British investigators, owing to more than 50 years of sharing at the base — which has an extensive history stretching back to 1945.

View 7 Images Armed police were pictured outside RAF Fairford today (Image: PA)

What is RAF Fairford?

RAF Fairford is one of 33 active RAF bases in the UK, and one of 12 where American personnel operate as part of the United States Visiting Force, making it an especially critical location when it comes to US-UK and US-European military cooperation.

The USVF is allowed to operate in several British bases under the Visiting Forces Act 1952, which was passed just eight years after Fairford was established in 1944.

View 7 Images Fairford is used as a critical entryway for Europe by the USAF (Image: SSgt. Madelyn Brown/USAF / SWNS)

What is the base used for?

Fairford is home to both American and British serving airmen and women, but is primarily known for hosting the 501st Combat Support Wing Headquarters and the 420th Air Base Squadron of the US Air Force (USAF). The base is the preferred bomber forward operating location in Europe for USAF's Global Strike Command.

As such, it has been used by the Trump administration as a critical base from which to launch bombing raids on Iran since March, following some early jostling about permissions when the operation started in February.

The administration has fielded both B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base during the conflict. Outside of military operations, the typically quiet site hosts up to 170,000 people every July during the Royal International Air Tattoo, the world's largest military air show.

View 7 Images RAF Fairford is the staging area for the Royal International Air Tattoo (RIAT) (Image: Cpl Phil Dye/RAF / SWNS)

Who has used RAF Fairford over the years?

RAF Fairford is an enduring symbol of American and British cooperation, and has been used by the two nations since troops trained for D-Day in 1944.

The US has assumed control of the base for much of its lifetime, until 1964, when this was briefly returned to the UK. Over eight years between 1969 and 1977, it served as a testing centre for the Concorde, which was developed by the British Aircraft Corporation (BAC), now BAE Systems.

The site has also served as a landing site for NASA's space shuttle, but since the Cold War has been primarily used by the US in a military capacity.

View 7 Images Fairford has been used by the USAF and RAF since 1944 (Image: Mirrorpix)

A brief history of RAF Fairford

1943: Wartime construction begins

1944: RAF Fairford opens, and supports D-Day operations on June 6 that year

1951: Control of the base is transferred to the USAF

1964: Base control returns briefly to the UK

1965: The UK's famed aerobatic team, the Red Arrows, forms at the base

1969 - 1977: BAC uses Fairford to test the Concord

1979: USAF resumes control of the base

1983: A NASA shuttle lands at Fairford while it is a designited landing abort site

1991: USAF uses Fairford as a staging base for B-52 bombers used in the First Gulf War

1999: USAF uses Fairford to stage NATO bombing of Yugoslavia

2003: USAF launches B-52s as part of Iraq war from Fairford

2019: Permanent rotational Lockheed U-2S Dragon Lady detachment is hosted at Fairford

March 2026: USAF uses base to deploy bombers during Operation Epic Fury

September 2026: Five men arrested at Fairford over suspected terror plot

View 7 Images Fairford has also previously hosted NASA aircraft (Image: Birmingham Post and Mail)

What have police said about the latest incident?

Police have said they are still working to fully understand the circumstances of the incident, with Assistant Chief Constable of Gloucestershire Police Richard Ocone said the service is in "constant contact" with local and international partners.

He said: "At around 12.45am today police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles travelling towards RAF Fairford.

"Armed officers responded and subsequently arrested five men in the Whelford area on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. The men were taken into custody where they remain. Counter Terrorism Policing are now leading the investigation.

"A 400m cordon has been put in place around the vehicles while the Army's Explosive Ordinance Disposal unit examine them.

‌



"As a precaution, around 85 households have been advised to evacuate while these examinations take place. A nearby leisure centre has been opened for those unable to stay with friends and family. The emergency services have well-rehearsed plans for dealing with major incidents.

"Work to establish the full nature of this incident is ongoing and we are in constant communication with our partners locally and nationally."

View 7 Images Donald Trump was quizzed about the operation (Image: AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

‌



What have locals said?

One woman who was evacuated said: "We were evacuated at 7am this morning. There was banging on the door and I answered in my nightie. An officer said a major incident was taking place near the airbase and we had to leave immediately.

"We've been here for hours and are just waiting for the police to update us, we were told it would be 1pm but we haven't heard anything yet."

Cotswold District Council Councillor Paul Hodgkinson said: "I'm at the leisure centre here in Cirencester where we've got a number of people evacuated. We think it's something around 50 people who have had to leave their homes today.

"I've spoken to quite a few of them and they're in pretty good spirits, but they just want to go home. We've had the airbase in the Cotswolds for years, it's been there in the village for many, many years. But with the conflict going on in the Middle East, we're certainly living with that now."

News.title: Nearly one million workers stuck in 'bogus self-employment' to benefit from abuses clampdown
News.content:
Nearly one million workers stuck in 'bogus self-employment' to benefit from abuses clampdown

EXCLUSIVE: Nearly a million workers stuck in 'bogus self-employment' that denies them basic rights are expected to benefit from a clampdown on abuses unveiled at Labour’s party conference

View 2 Images The proposals could help workers such as parcel couriers, delivery drivers and gig economy workers (Image: Getty Images)

Nearly a million workers stuck in “bogus self-employment” that denies them basic rights are expected to benefit from a clampdown on abuses unveiled at Labour’s party conference.

‌



Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds will on Monday vow to close loopholes that allow bosses to avoid statutory obligations, such as paying the National Minimum Wage or holiday pay, to workers. As many as 900,000 people may currently be affected by “bogus self-employment” practices.

‌



Mr Reynolds is expected to confirm a formal consultation, due to be published in the coming weeks, on how to give greater legal certainty to workers and potentially extend core employment rights to those often excluded from them.

‌



Labour conference live: Andy Burnham to face questions on future of Britain as poll boosts party READ MORE :

Andy Burnham says he is more determined to fix social care after death of his father READ MORE :

View 2 Images Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds will on Monday vow to close loopholes that allow bosses to avoid statutory obligations (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

His announcement will also include a package of extra rights for the genuinely self-employed, including greater health and safety protections, action on blacklisting and a new right to a written statement for certain self-employed individuals as outlined in the Labour’s Plan to Make Work Pay.

In his speech at Labour’s conference in Liverpool, the Cabinet minister is expected to say: “There is one area which both workers and businesses raise with me repeatedly and that is bogus self-employment. It denies workers basic employment rights, undercuts businesses who are doing the right thing, and leaves people with the sense that playing by the rules doesn’t pay.

‌



“Everyone can see this isn’t right. It is a fundamental question of fairness and Conference, I tell you now, we will put an end to it.”

The consultation, which will launch when Parliament returns from Conference recess next month, is expected to consider proposals to have a legal assumption of worker status when a case is brought to tribunal.

It will look at de-emphasising the personal service test when assessing status in order to clamp-down on misuse of substitution clauses.

‌



This could help workers such as parcel couriers, delivery drivers and gig economy workers.

TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak said: “For too long cynical bosses have been able to exploit gaps in the law to deny workers proper pay and conditions. They’ve relied on sham contracts drawn up by expensive lawyers to classify workers as self-employed.

“Not anymore. Today’s announcement paves the way towards closing these dodgy legal loopholes – ensuring workers get the pay and treatment they are owed.

Article continues below

“It will also make it harder for bad faith employers to use bogus self-employment to sidestep their obligation to offer guaranteed hours contracts to workers as some have threatened.

“Along with stronger rights for the genuinely self-employed, this is a major step forward for workers in every corner of the country.”

On single status of worker, Mr Nowak added: “To finish the job and ensure all workers get the pay and protection they deserve, the government should now set out a timetable to deliver a single status of worker."

News.title: Five arrested as counter-terror police investigate major incident near RAF Fairford
News.content:
Five men have been arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act and explosive offences after three "suspicious vehicles" were reported travelling towards an RAF base, police have said.

A major incident was declared and dozens of homes near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire were evacuated following the report at about 00:45 BST on Sunday.

An Army explosive ordnance disposal team has been examining vehicles near the base, which is used by the United States Air Force (USAF), as counter-terror police lead the investigation.

Residents evacuated from the nearby village of Whelford have been told they will not be able to return home overnight, but officials say they believe the incident is contained.

Aerial pictures showed a remote-controlled robot approaching stationary white vans in a wooded area, though its use has not been confirmed by police.

A 400m cordon has been placed around the area, where a hazardous area response team was deployed as part of a major emergency service response.

News.title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe
News.content:
Five men have been arrested on suspicion of explosive and terrorism offences after a major incident was declared at an airbase in the west of England.

Bomb disposal teams have been examining a number of vehicles near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire and dozens of homes in the surrounding area have been evacuated.

Here is a summary of what we know so far.

News.title: Burnham proposes NHS-style social care system for England
News.content:
Andy Burnham wants to offer access to free social care services to everyone in England, and will put his plans before voters at the next general election.

The prime minister told the BBC that it would be a system in which "everyone contributes, everyone is covered". He did not rule out tax rises, acknowledging it may be "difficult or unpopular" with some.

Burnham said he wants to set out his "vision" on Tuesday and Whitehall troubleshooter Baroness Casey, who is conducting a review, will advise on the "best way of doing it".

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp said the PM was suggesting Labour wanted "more tax rises" to pay for the reforms, adding the Conservatives would not support this.

Burnham has made reforming social care one of his flagship policies and has spoken of the experience of his father Roy, who had Alzheimer's and died earlier this month.

While he has been clear on his ambition to make changes to the system, he has yet to explain how any changes would be funded.

Adult social care provides state support to help people live more independently, including assistance at home.

Unlike the NHS, social care is not free at the point of use. In England and Northern Ireland, people with savings worth more than Â£23,250 are not entitled to help with care costs from their council.

In Wales and Scotland, different rules apply in terms of eligibility.

Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, the prime minister said: "I am talking about a system that works on NHS principles because that is the only way you can make it work.

"There is free personal care elsewhere in the UK. I don't think it's right that people in England don't get the same and it's not something we're going to rush."

Personal care offered in Scotland is available to all adults who are assessed as needing help with tasks including eating and bathing.

News.title: Orange Order march row goes to heart of ongoing divisions in Northern Ireland
News.content:
History shows that when the politics of Northern Ireland are wrapped up in a street dispute, friction is seldom far away.

Bitter rows in the Stormont chamber between unionists and nationalists happen almost every week, but ground-level arguments are rare these days.

The Drumcree parade dispute in Portadown is a clash of political cultures.

The Orange Order is a Protestant pro-British organisation. The area where it wants to walk is largely Catholic, and predominantly inhabited by pro-Irish nationalists.

This dispute over a piece of road is not just a local problem. It has the potential to affect other parts of Northern Ireland and the power-sharing arrangements at Stormont.

"What happens at Drumcree never stays at Drumcree," was how one retired politician put it.

News.title: Inside Yemen's front-line city as Houthis battle for control
News.content:
"This is the first drone," said the soldier accompanying us in south-western Yemen. "It's usually followed by an attack."

The buzzing sound overhead got louder as we took cover under the bushes, before climbing back into the vehicle and driving away.

Within about 10 minutes, the loud thuds of strikes followed, one after another, though it was unclear where they landed.

It is hard to tell where the front line begins in the mountains south-west of the city of Taiz.

Saudi-backed pro-government forces are battling to push back Houthi fighters, who swept down the coast of the Red Sea earlier this month, taking control of a key shipping chokepoint and escalating Yemen's civil war.

We travelled with government forces from Taiz through checkpoints to the line where their control ends and no man's land begins, in order to see the fighting up close.

News.title: No handshakes between Republic of Ireland and Israel
News.content:
The Republic of Ireland and Israel players did not shake hands with each other before or after Sunday's controversial Uefa Nations League game in Hungary.

After walking on to the pitch at Nagyerdei Stadion, the Republic of Ireland squad stood for their national anthem and bowed their heads before Israel's anthem.

Following the anthems, the two teams did not line up for the traditional handshakes.

There was also no exchange of pennants between Republic of Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel skipper Manor Solomon, who did not shake hands.

The fixtures have been embroiled in controversy since February when the two teams were drawn to play each other in Group B3.

The Republic of Ireland players have faced calls to withdraw from the games because of the ongoing Israel-Gaza war with a "Stop The Game" campaign - organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine - gathering pace.

However, the players voted to fulfil the fixture during a lengthy meeting at the team's hotel in Debrecen on Saturday.

Later on Saturday, goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu confirmed he had withdrawn from the squad, saying he felt it "would be wrong to participate" in Sunday's game and the return fixture in the Serbian town of Backa Topola on 4 October.

The Irish players wore black armbands, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said on Saturday was a gesture "in recognition of all lives lost in the [Gaza] conflict".

After scoring the Republic of Ireland's third goal in a 3-0 win, Jack Moylan removed his armband and kissed it before kissing his team's badge.

The Republic of Ireland players were jeered by the small number of Israel fans in attendance when they emerged for their pre-game warm-up.

While the FAI confirmed no tickets would be sold to Republic of Ireland supporters, a handful of fans were spotted inside the stadium.

News.title: Ten NHS staff removed over Noah Woods data breach
News.content:
Ten NHS staff have been removed from duty or suspended after a data breach involving the digital medical records of three-year-old Noah Woods.

Launching an "urgent" investigation, Dr Martin Mansfield, deputy chief medical officer at East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust, said that any unauthorised access of patient data was "completely unacceptable".

The trust has apologised "unreservedly" to Noah's family and said disciplinary action would be taken if needed.

A major search for Noah was carried out in the village of Brantham, Suffolk, after the child went missing on 15 September. His body was found the next day in a nearby pond by police divers.

A spokesperson for the trust said 10 employees had been "removed from active duty or suspended whilst investigations are concluded".

It comes after Sir Jim Mackey, the chief executive of NHS England, wrote to every trust on Friday, ordering stronger measures to tackle data breaches.

"We have seen too many cases of people abusing that trust, and enough is enough," said Sir Jim.

"Anyone who thinks they can satisfy their curiosity by looking at a patient's record should know this: they will be found out, they may lose their career and could end up with a criminal record."

News.title: England win series as Banton delivers on potential
News.content:
Third Metro Bank one-day international, Kia Oval

England 355-7 (50 overs): Banton 126, Brook 77, Cox 76

Sri Lanka 132 (29.1 overs): Kusal 35; Dawson 3-26

England won by 223 runs

Scorecard

Tom Banton delivered on all of his potential by crashing a brilliant first international century as England wrapped up their summer with an ODI series win over Sri Lanka.

The 27-year-old right-hander was once the rising star of English cricket when handed a debut in 2019 but afterwards fell out of love with the game after losing his way.

After reaching his hundred in 95 balls in the third one-day international at The Oval, he stood with arms wide and looked to the sky - all of that disappointment seemingly behind him.

"My fiance, Lilly, was here and all of her family," Banton said.

"Unfortunately, my mum, dad and brother weren't here because whenever my mum seems to come I don't do that well.

"Bless her, she is not banned from coming, but she avoids coming now."

The opener went on to make 126 from 105 deliveries, perfectly countering tricky early conditions - conditions in which Joe Root struggled uncharacteristically for 18 from 37 balls - and going on to share an increasingly aggressive stand of 150 in 117 balls with captain Harry Brook.

"To score a hundred for England is just the best feeling on earth," Banton said. "I don't think anything is going to beat it."

Brook made 77 and Jordan Cox, picked in the place of the injured Jos Buttler, added a 52-ball 76 to lift England to 355-7.

That always appeared a match-winning total on a surface offering bounce for the pace bowlers and turn for the spinners.

Sri Lanka crumbled to 132 all out in 29.1 overs, giving England a 223-run win and their biggest ODI victory against the tourists.

It meant England signed off their summer, one that included off-field issues, the end of Bazball, Ben Stokes' retirement and Root's surprise return as Test skipper, with a fifth successive series win amid the madness across formats.

News.title: More questions than answers after major incident near RAF Fairford
News.content:
But some eyes, too, have turned to Moscow.

Danish intelligence warned last week Russia could in the coming months launch a limited military attack on a Nato country.

Germany has already formally accused Russia of using a drone carrying explosives in an attempted attack on Leipzig in August.

Over the summer, the Russian embassy in London warned the UK against allowing Ukraine to use British drones deep inside Russian territory: "The deeper [the UK's] involvement in the conflict and the greater its support for Kyiv's terrorist machinery, the higher price it will pay."

That, too, was seen as a direct threat.

There are also possibilities of some kind of Islamist attack, or even an incident of direct action by a group opposed to both the US-Israeli war on Iran or the use of UK bases to launch strikes.

One central question is whether the authorities were prepared for such an attack.

The US handles security within the base; the UK is responsible all threats outside the perimeter. What did the authorities know?

President Trump said the suspects had been under investigation "for a long time".

But there are also suggestions the incident was foiled only because a passing driver reported strange vans to the police.

At the time of the explicit Iranian threat against the UK, a spokesman for the Ministry of Defence said: "Our armed forces are ready to keep the United Kingdom safe from any kind of attacks, whether it's on our soil or from abroad. The UK stands ready 24/7 to defend itself."

So for now, there remain more questions that facts.

Was a hostile foreign state involved, or were proxies acting on its behalf? What was intended and what was the potential risk to local people?

One thing is clear: the threat from conflicts involving the UK will not always stay overseas.

News.title: More than 50 arrested at Palestine Action support rally
News.content:
Merseyside Police said more than 50 people had so far been detained at the Defend Our Juries event and that officers were in the process of making arrests on suspicion of wearing/carrying an article supporting a proscribed organisation.

A force spokesperson said it respected everyone's rights to protest lawfully while also aiming to keep the peace and ensure public safety.

The force said it made "detailed and co-ordinated plans ahead of such events to ensure it can apply this consistently, fairly and proportionately".

The spokesperson said not everyone present at the protest had been committing a criminal offence.

The arrests were criticised by Amnesty International, which called them a "shameful attack on freedom of speech".

One of those detained was human rights barrister Margaret Owen, 94.

A spokesperson for Defend Our Juries said: "We had hoped the new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, would do the sensible thing and bin the ban on Palestine Action given the weight of public pressure to do so and the escalating amount of resources required in enforcing it.

"Continuing the charade of the proscription of Palestine Action is illogical, unsustainable and immoral."

News.title: Thousands affected and roads closed after burst pipe
News.content:
Thousands of homes in parts of West Sussex have water supply issues and a number of roads have flooded after what police are describing as a "significant" leak.

Roads around the Southgate Roundabout in Crawley have been closed on Sunday morning due to the burst water pipe, Sussex Police said.

Southern Water said about 9,000 customers were impacted, but as of 19:45 BST, most customers had seen their supplies restored.

A company spokesperson said: "Our teams are on site and working as quickly and safely as possible to repair the burst and restore supplies."

The company said customers were experiencing a loss of water supply or low pressure in the following areas - Woolborough Road, Holmcroft, Southgate, Tilgate and Furnace Green.

It first reported at 12:00 that supplies had returned to some homes.

Southern Water said its teams were still carrying out repairs but the damaged section of pipe had been removed and its replacement installed.

"We apologise for this disruption and would like to thank customers for their patience while we complete the repair," it added.

John Boulton, who is 82, and his partner were without water earlier.

He said: "It's pretty disgusting, really - we pay so much for the water supply."

Boulton said he had just paid Â£22 for bottled water in a shop.

News.title: Murder probe as cyclist dies following moped crash
News.content:
A murder inquiry has begun after an e-bike cyclist died following a collision with a moped in west London.

Emergency services were called to North Pole Road, North Kensington, at about 01:20 BST on Friday where the seriously injured 24-year-old man was found. He was pronounced dead at the scene shortly after.

Police said the investigation was at an early stage but it was believed the moped had been pursuing the e-bike cyclist prior to the crash.

Dt Ch Insp Neil John said detectives were "pursuing a number of lines of inquiry, including efforts to identify and trace the rider of the moped".

"Our thoughts are with the victim's family at what is a very difficult time," he added.

"We have launched a full investigation and are working hard to get answers and establish exactly what happened.

"As part of this, we're urging anyone who was in the area at the time and may have seen the e-bike or the moped to get in touch with us as soon as possible. If you have any information that could help, please come forward."

News.title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos
News.content:
Traitors star Paul Gorton did not think twice about sharing photographs on social media while enjoying a family holiday with his wife and two young children.

But when he returned home he discovered that his house in Cheshire had been burgled just days earlier.

"The eerie bit is at 21:10 BST I posted that me and Kate were by the side of the pool, we've got full bellies, the kids are in bed, we're actually having our little bit of the holiday," he said.

"About 20 minutes later, little did we know, our house has been broken into."

Paul's bike as well as several sentimental items including an irreplaceable ring from Kate's grandmother were stolen in the burglary on 28 August.

The perpetrators managed to break in through the bi-fold doors at the back of the house by using a technique known as lock snapping before cutting the broadband connection.

News.title: Man charged with murdering woman in Darlington
News.content:
A man has been charged with murdering a woman who was found dead by police.

Andrew Bell, 44, of Darlington, is accused of killing Leanne Park, 44, in the town on Wednesday.

Durham Police said she was pronounced dead at an address in Parkgate at about 21:15 BST. Her family said she was the "best mam, nana, daughter and friend we could wish for".

Bell is due to appear at Newton Aycliffe Magistrates' Court on Monday.

A 27-year-old man arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender has been released on bail, the force said.

A spokesperson said crime scene investigators would continue to work at the scene and a police cordon was "expected to remain in place for some time".

Anyone with information about the murder is urged to contact detectives.

Follow BBC Tees on X,, external Facebook, external, Nextdoor and Instagram, external and listen to Radio Tees on BBC Sounds.

News.title: Police get more time to quiz suspects in alleged plot against Jewish community
News.content:
Detectives have been granted an extra week to question two men arrested as part of an investigation into an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester.

The extension means the men - both in the 30s - can now be detained until 4 October.

The men were arrested in the Northern Quarter area of Manchester on 20 September - the eve of Yom Kippur, when thousands of British Jews were in synagogues.

A spokesperson for the Metropolitan Police, which is leading the investigation, said their work was "ongoing and officers continue to pursue a number of lines of enquiry".

News.title: Your pictures of the Harvest Moon shimmering across the UK sky
News.content:
September's full Moon glowed across the UK sky on Saturday and many people seemed to have perfect conditions for viewing it.

It's also known as the Harvest Moon because of its association with the time of year people traditionally gather crops.

The Moon reached its fullest point at 17:49 BST on Saturday but it was later, when the sky got darker, that it made its biggest impact.

BBC Weather Watchers have been submitting the photos they took and here are a few of our favourites of those submitted so far.

News.title: Trump’s new doomsday ad warns NFL fans of ‘final battle’ for America — at taxpayer expense
News.content:

A second ad promoting President Donald Trump that was “paid for by the U.S. government” aired during NFL games Sunday — warning American football fans of a “final battle” for the country.

“This is the final battle with you at my side,” Trump says in the ad, which features him walking down a hallway as suspenseful music plays.

“We will cast out the communists, Marxists and fascists. We will throw off the sick political class that hates our country. We will rout the fake news media, and we will liberate America from these villains once and for all,” Trump said.

The ad aired during Fox’s broadcasts of the Washington Commanders game against the Seattle Seahawks and the match-up between the Carolina Panthers and Cleveland Browns, according to CNN.

The Trump administration is already facing criticism over airing ads featuring the president that explicitly state they were “paid for by the U.S. government” — just a little over a month before the midterm elections.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump appeared in an ad Sunday that vowed to ‘throw off the sick political class that hates our country’ ( U.S. Government )

The White House compared the ads to previous administrations running public service announcements about Medicare or the Covid vaccination, telling CNN in a statement the commercials “are very clearly not campaign ads.” The Independent contacted the White House Sunday for further clarification.

The ad is nearly identical to a video Trump shared on Truth Social in January 2024, during his third presidential campaign. That version of the video includes a message to “join President Trump’s Fight for America” and information about his campaign.

It comes as the Trump administration faces criticism over several other government-funded ads that have recently aired featuring the president.

An intense ad titled “America Will Never Be a Communist Country” that aired Thursday also raised eyebrows. It came amid the Trump administration’s ban on MS NOW, CNN and Politico and the subsequent launching of its own media operation, which critics slammed as “state-run media.”

That commercial begins with a series of black-and-white images of Trump before cutting to images of him at political rallies and White House events. The commercial promises to “defeat communism, socialism and Marxism” and boasts Trump’s “largest tax cuts in history” while vowing to “defend law and order and police.”

open image in gallery The commercial, which aired during at least two NFL games Sunday, is nearly identical to a campaign video Trump shared on Truth Social in 2024 while he was running for president for a third time ( U.S. Government )

It also featured a message from UFC CEO Dana White praising Trump as the “toughest, most resilient person” he has met.

Critics slammed the commercial, which also appeared on Fox, saying it clearly resembled propaganda.

“Took this one right out of the Florida Republican playbook,” said Nikki Fried, chair of the Florida Democrats. “This ad is pure communist propaganda. The pure collapse of Trump.”

“Hold the party that condones this responsible in November,” said Joyce Alene, a former U.S. attorney appointed by former President Barack Obama.

White House officials defended the earlier ad in a statement to The Independent Thursday, saying that since Trump is not on the ballot, the ads are not campaign related.

“These public service announcements are about reminding Americans to love their country and understand what makes it worth defending, at home, at our borders, and abroad,” the spokesperson said. “The ad is educational and unapologetically patriotic. We should be proud of our country.”

Andy Burnham said that “broken” social care will eventually break the NHS as he outlined his plans to reform the system.

At the Labour Party conference in Liverpool, the prime minister will pledge that his government will bring about radical change for Britain, and he told the BBC he would “grasp the nettle” of social care reform in England.

The former Greater Manchester mayor said he would put his plan for a national care service along the lines of the NHS, funded by the taxpayer and free at the point of use, to the public at the next general election.

Mr Burnham, whose father died earlier this month, told the BBC’s Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg: “For me, obviously, coming in to this journey as prime minister as my dad was ending his, has been hard.

“But it pushes me on, and I’m going to grasp the nettle on social care.”

He described social care in England as being as “unfair as American healthcare, where the most vulnerable in society can lose everything.”

As the conference began in earnest on Sunday, Merseyside Police arrested two demonstrators outside it during a protest in support of Palestine Action.

Dancing With the Stars co-host Julianne Hough has shared how she plans to bring her ballroom skills to Broadway in a new revival of Damn Yankees.

An Emmy Award winner for her DWTS choreography, Hough will star alongside Tony and Emmy winner Neil Patrick Harris and Austin Scott in the first production of the musical in more than 30 years, slated for an April 2027 opening night. She’ll take on the role of Lola, originated onstage in 1955 and in the 1958 film version by Gwen Verdon, who is widely regarded as one of Broadway’s finest dancers.

Asked by The Independent at a press conference announcing the revival which of her ballroom skills she feels will benefit her in one of the most iconic dance roles in Broadway history, Hough said, “I think the partnership and the family.”

“The greatest thing about being a part of Dancing With the Stars for the last 20 years — I’ve been on and off that show as a pro, a judge, and a host — it’s family. We have each other’s backs,” she continued.

Hough talked about the “friction” that the show is experiencing after season 35 kicked off earlier this month after fans complained about the cast including celebrities with previous dance experience. “It’s almost welcomed because it allows people to have an opinion,” she said. “It allows people to have their own unique thought process about something.

open image in gallery Austin Scott, Julianne Hough, and Neil Patrick Harris will star in 'Damn Yankees' on Broadway ( Emilio Madrid )

open image in gallery Julianne Hough is returning to Broadway in 2027 in one of the most iconic dance roles in Broadway history ( Reuters )

“So the idea of bridging that world where we spent the last 20 years educating people on what a Cha Cha was and a Pasa Doble ... we were able to really nurture and love the people, and feel so grateful for the fans that have followed us.”

Hough called it an “honor” and “privilege” to have a career that has led her “into new sectors that keep art alive.”

In addition to her time on Dancing With the Stars — including two Mirrorball Trophy wins — Hough previously appeared on Broadway in the 2022 play POTUS: Or, Behind Every Great Dumbass Are Seven Women Trying to Keep Him Alive. She also starred in the films Burlesque (2010), Footloose (2011), and Rock of Ages (2012). Most recently, she returned to the big screen in The Bride.

Hough’s dance skills will be put to the test in Damn Yankees, which will feature direction and choreography by Tony winner Sergio Trujillo. Scott, as a self-proclaimed “mover” and not necessarily a dancer, voiced how thrilled he was to be working with someone like Hough who knows the ropes.

“Knowing that I have a partner who has a lot of experience, literally dancing with people who have no idea how to dance, is a huge comfort,” Scott said at the press conference.

A popular story about a lesbian bar in Massachusetts has gone so viral that Hollywood studios are now considering potential adaptations for the article, according to an industry report.

On September 22, the Boston Globe published the piece in question, titled “A Western Mass. lesbian bar required KN-95 masks. When it changed the rules, all hell broke loose.” The article, written by Annalisa Quinn, quickly became a hot topic on social media feeds and sparked online discussions and think pieces on all corners of the internet — and the buzzy conversation has apparently made its way over to film and TV executives.

According to a new report from The Hollywood Reporter, talent agency UTA “has been fielding inquiries about potential adaptations for the article — both in the scripted space and the documentary sphere.” UTA represents the Globe.

A spokesperson for the newspaper told THR: “This story has certainly resonated with a wide range of audiences nationally and internationally. It is now one of the most-read stories we’ve published, and has already garnered many thousands of subscriptions.”

The Independent has reached out to the Globe and UTA for comment.

open image in gallery The Boston Globe is reportedly fielding inquiries regarding a potential adaptation of its recent viral article ( Getty Images )

The article follows a lesbian establishment, Last Ditch Bar, in Greenfield, Massachusetts, that faced chaos after lifting its mask mandate.

Bartenders announced in an Instagram post issued to the “immunocompromised disabled divas” in August that patrons no longer had to wear KN95 masks on Saturday nights.

The decision was met with backlash and accused of being “complicit in a mass disabling event.”

Quinn’s article was praised online for its relaying of the dramatic saga, which was complete with zinger one-liner quotes from scorned customers as well as sympathetic details about the bar owner who is in a mountain of debt because of the crisis.

open image in gallery 2015 movie ‘Spotlight’ was based on the Boston Globe’s investigative reporting ( Kerry Hayes )

It quickly became one of the most read stories in the newspaper’s history, with a leaked staffer memo reporting that more than a thousand new subscribers flocked to the Globe in less than a day after the story was published.

The viral article’s success is notable considering the stark contrast in subject matter of other monumental articles in the Globe’s history that have been adapted.

In the early 2000s, the newspaper published a Pulitzer Prize-winning series of bombshell articles that exposed the systemic cover-up of abuse within the Catholic Church. The journalism inspired the 2015 Academy Award-winning film Spotlight.

Years later, the paper’s investigative reporting on the crimes and death of former New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez also led to the podcast Gladiator: Aaron Hernandez. The podcast eventually led to scripted FX series American Sports Story: Aaron Hernandez, which was executive produced by Ryan Murphy.
