Microsoft founder Bill Gates has warned that emergency cutoffs for artificial intelligence — the so-called “kill switch” — are not enough on their own and that the technology is powerful enough to cause 1 billion deaths.

The billionaire philanthropist argued that internal monitoring and built-in safety mechanisms are far more critical than emergency shut-off tools.

“It’s not enough to have a kill switch,” Gates told NBC’s “Meet the Press” Sunday. “I would never want to say I’m against a kill switch. But when you’re trying to moderate the bad behavior, you need insight and records of what’s being done.”

He pointed directly to the threat of AI-driven terrorism.

“AI is certainly powerful enough to drive events that cause a billion deaths,” he warned. “So even though it’s pretty hard to get to 100% [of humanity], there’s never been a weapon as powerful as the combination of people with ill intent using the latest AI tools.”

open image in gallery Bill Gates speaks to Kristen Welker from Meet The Press in a new wide-ranging interview about AI and the race between the US and China ( NBC )

Gates dismissed concerns that AI safety rules would slow U.S. tech companies down, directly responding to President Donald Trump’s stance that government regulation would handicap American innovation in its race against China.

“What he said is fine,” Gates said, referring to Trump. “But I think after he hears from me and other people, including that this does not handicap us in whatever he thinks the nation-state race is, that, you know, we will come to a consensus.”

Gates urged Washington to mandate active tracking of models’ behavior within labs, adding that regulating AIcould prove harder than Cold War nuclear treaty negotiations.

“This is more difficult than that was,” he noted.

Gates said the most pressing threat comes from bad actors using current AI tools to carry out cyberattacks, scramble bank accounts or shut down power grids, rather than rogue autonomous machines.

“Now, small groups with AI can do what only the biggest countries could do,” Gates said. “So it’s really the bad intent plus AI that looms as a major threat. Unless governments insist on various safeguards, you know, we will see a lot of big, negative things because we’re not safeguarding.”

open image in gallery Gates addressed Donald Trump’s race-to-win approach with China, arguing that internal safety limits will not slow down American tech companies — following a summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the White House confirmed that both nations established a working dialogue to assess AI risks ( Getty )

Trump has pushed back on federal intervention in AI development, writing on Truth Social earlier this month: “WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so.”

Gates emphasized that the U.S. has a history of driving global consensus on safety standards, pointing to past international agreements on aviation safety, environmental policy and nuclear arms.

“And AI is one we’re going to have to go back to this, ‘Hey, humanity is all in this together,’” he said.

His warnings echo concerns across the tech industry and from AI developers themselves. Anthropic whistleblower Jacob Coxon recently warned that “the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

Top industry executives, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, have also acknowledged the need to manage the speed of development. Amodei wrote in a recent blog post that leading companies should coordinate safety standards internationally while maintaining a competitive advantage over China.

open image in gallery Tech executives, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, and former industry insiders agree that development speeds must be managed as companies push for international safety standards ( Reuters )

Lawmakers have also pushed for joint rules with foreign powers. Democratic Representative Ro Khanna of California told NBC that Washington and Beijing should set up a joint technical working group, arguing that banning self-improving AI models “should not be controversial.”

“I do believe the United States can lead on a treaty that is both enforceable and verifiable, where we ban recursive, self-improving AI, and we have some monitoring of these frontier labs,” Khanna told the outlet.

Following this week’s summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the White House confirmed that the two nations established a working dialogue to assess AI risks, with additional talks planned.

During the NBC interview, Gates also addressed questions about his past ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein after unsealed Justice Department documents renewed attention on their relationship.

“I was told by Jeffrey after I met him that he could help raise billions of dollars for global health — you know, he wouldn’t be paid, he would have no role,” Gates said. “That proved to be a complete dead end. So my spending time with him, like many other people, kind of helped his reputation. You know, that’s very regrettable.”

White House Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino is facing fierce backlash — even from fellow Republicans — over a social media post depicting him in a tuxedo, sloshing champagne with some glamorous party pals as Americans grapple with a deepening cost-of-living crisis linked to the Iran War and the Trump administration’s tariffs.

Scavino shared the apparent AI-generated video depicting him and who appears to be his second wife, Erin Elmore, and Lara Trump, grinning in ballgowns while they are pushed on a gold luggage cart through the White House by Eric Trump to Pitbull’s “Don’t Stop the Party.” Gold confetti falls before a jubilant President Donald Trump enters the scene.

“This is not an intended for the Dems heads to explode — Being some of the post State Dinner party has gotten out, I felt inclined to share mine as well, in complete transparency, with the American People. GOD BLESS THE USA!!!” Scavino, 50, posted.

However, it wasn’t just Democrats who had a knee-jerk reaction to the post, which comes as Trump’s poll numbers continue to plummet ahead of the November midterms.

“You really have no shame, do you? Many Americans can’t afford groceries, gas or their mortgage payment, and you post a tone deaf AI video of you and your buddies partying at the People’s House,” conservative activist Carrie Prejean Boller wrote.

open image in gallery An apparent AI-generated video by White House Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino showed him partying and spraying champagne with some glamorous companions ( Dan Scavino/X )

“One of my friends couldn’t afford air conditioner this summer,” Meghan McCain, conservative commentator and daughter of late Republican Senator John McCain, commented on the video.

Jonah Goldberg, editor-in-chief of center-right publication The Dispatch, quipped: “This is precisely the midterm messaging the GOP needs from the Deputy White House Chief of Staff.”

Sarah Longwell, an anti-Trump Republican who founded the Bulwark, called it “Real fall of Rome s***.”

Other self-described MAGA accounts on X also slammed the video. One X user wrote: “Wow... This is really going to resonate with everyday Americans. They are so out of touch. It's astonishing.”

“Very relatable to Americans who are getting crushed by inflation, gas prices & cost of living,” another noted.

CNN anchor Jake Tapper also reshared the post, simply noting: “WH deputy chief of staff.”

open image in gallery Scavino, the White House’s deputy chief of staff, later shared another AI-generated video showing Trump and other White House officials partying at the White House with Chinese President Xi Jinping after the State Dinner ( AFP/Getty )

Scavino appeared to lean into the controversy by resharing another AI-generated video that showed a rowdy party after the State Dinner at the White House. The images depict Trump, Elon Musk, Marco Rubio and other officials partying with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Scavino wrote “...as the typical nutters are losing their s*** over AI created content, well done! It is AI, correct?”

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

There is little over a month to go until the midterm elections. New polling from NBC News shows Democrats with a 9-point advantage over Republicans when it comes to taking control of Congress. Decision Desk HQ forecasts a 72 percent probability of Democrats taking control of the House and a 54 percent probability of the party winning the Senate.

President Donald Trump is facing the worst approval rating of his second term at just 32 percent, according to Reuters.

open image in gallery China's President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump speak through interpreters while First Lady Melania Trump talks with Tesla CEO Elon Musk at a State Dinner in Washington, D.C. last week ( AFP/Getty )

Trump campaigned in 2024 on lowering costs for everyday Americans and not starting any new wars but the U.S. conflict with Iran has led to elevated prices at gas pump, grocery store and across a plethora of everyday essentials.

The president has undertaken a number of taxpayer-funded lavish renovations at the White House including breaking ground on a $600 million ballroom.

A recent Politico poll showed 53 percent of Americans couldn’t recall struggling harder to make ends meet — and 46 percent said they felt that Trump was fully or mostly responsible for the state of the economy.

Democrats have hammered Republicans by campaigning on the cost of living crisis ahead of the November midterms - and at least some in the Republican party have taken note.

Senator Jim Justice, a West Virginia Republican, openly criticized his party’s current approach.

“You’ve got Republicans scrambling everywhere,” Justice told The New York Post this week. “When — my lord of living, all we had to do was really be in touch with the people four or five months ago … We’ve done all kinds of great stuff. You know, but we’re tone deaf in a lot of ways.”

The Northern Ireland Secretary has appealed for calm while urging political and community leaders to reach for compromise to resolve a tense parading stand-off in Portadown.

The plea from Sir Chris Bryant came as thousands of demonstrators maintained a blockade along the largely nationalist Garvaghy Road in Portadown, seeking to block a controversial Orange Order march from taking place.

Accusations of unlawful conduct were levelled by unionist politicians after Northern Ireland’s First Minister Michelle O’Neill and senior colleagues attended the demonstration on Sunday.

Regional legislation governing public processions dictates that any counter-protests must be submitted to and approved by the Parades Commission.

Because the demonstration along Garvaghy Road was not officially notified, it constitutes an unauthorised gathering. Under their pledge of office, Ms O’Neill and fellow ministers in the Stormont Executive are required to uphold the law.

open image in gallery Orangemen and supporters being blocked by police at Drumcree church on September 27, 2026 in Portadown, Northern Ireland ( Getty )

Police officers spent Sunday using loudspeakers to warn demonstrators that blocking the public highway made them subject to arrest.

Addressing the crowd on Sunday evening, Ms O’Neill told those gathered to "stay the course" and remain present until midnight at the earliest.

DUP leader Gavin Robinson insisted that members of Sinn Féin ought to be held accountable for their conduct.

Speaking to reporters in Belfast on Sunday afternoon, he said: "We can’t have a situation where people who have the privilege of holding high office in Northern Ireland so flagrantly disregard the pledge of office and statutory underpinnings of their office,"

An earlier determination by the Parades Commission authorizing the Orange Order procession to march past Drumcree Church and along Garvaghy Road was upheld by the High Court in Belfast during an "unprecedented" early morning session on Sunday.

Having been linked to major civil unrest during the Troubles, the Drumcree parade has faced a prohibition since 1998.

Heavy rain fell on Sunday morning as large groups of protesters, many wearing balaclavas, gathered along the route, delaying the procession’s planned 8am commencement.

The impasse persisted throughout the day and into the evening, with Orangemen gathered roughly a mile away at Drumcree Church awaiting clearance to march.

At approximately 6pm, a group of Orangemen exited the church hall and walked down the hill before being stopped by police. Officers advised senior representatives that commission rules strictly capped attendance on the hill at 35 people.

open image in gallery Protesters on Garvaghy Road in Portadown ( Reuters )

A gathering of supporters assembled alongside the Orangemen.

The growing political conflict surrounding the march now threatens to destabilise the powersharing administration in Belfast.

When questioned if his party would continue sharing power with Sinn Féin—a move where a withdrawal by either side would trigger the collapse of the devolved executive—Mr Robinson addressed the situation directly.

"Our party is maintaining the dignity of the Portadown Orangemen as they have shown determination and patience so will we," Mr Robinson stated.

He added: "I can look at you all in the eye today and say we are being plunged into difficult territory because of the actions of people who are expected to be lawmakers in our country breaking the law.

"The fundamental principle of upholding the rule of law in this society are sacrosanct and cannot be tarnished."

Earlier on Garvaghy Road, Sinn Féin vice-president Ms O’Neill informed journalists that reigniting the debate around Drumcree "brings into question how this whole peace process works".

Meanwhile, party president Mary Lou McDonald urged Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris to intervene directly and halt the parade.

She asserted that residents living near Garvaghy Road would "not be drawn back to the past".

"The Secretary of State needs to intervene. The chief constable of the PSNI needs to intervene and put a stop to this," she remarked.

open image in gallery A demonstrator holds a placard as people protest on the Garvaghy Road ( Reuters )

Under current legislation, the Northern Ireland Secretary holds authority to stop a parade should the chief constable request an intervention over fears of severe public disorder.

Sir Chris travelled to Northern Ireland on Sunday from the Labour Party conference in Liverpool to conduct emergency talks with key political figures.

In statements to reporters in Belfast, Sir Chris remarked that "nobody wants to go back 28 years".

He stated: "The whole idea of us coming here is to be able to try and be able to talk specifically face to face to some of the political leaders and some of the community leaders to see if we can get to a settled position,"

He added: "The truth is everybody has to double down on compromise – that’s what life’s all about – double down on compromise."

Police Service of Northern Ireland chief constable Jon Boutcher called upon all sides to collaborate in resolving the ongoing dispute.

He noted that the police operation was collecting evidence regarding "whatever has been happening from whatever party".

"I am hoping we will bring all of today’s events to a sensible and peaceful conclusion," he remarked.

Regarding a potential resolution, he said: "There has got to be a longer-term conversation which involves politicians and the people involved in what we have seen in the last 24 hours, trying to find a space that they can resolve these issues."

He noted that several "sensible voices" urging restraint had been "listened to by all parties".

Prime Minister Andy Burnham made an appeal for "calm on all sides", adding that "big gains made in Northern Ireland, and we don’t want to see things go backwards".

open image in gallery The Orange Order has not been permitted to march on Garvaghy Road for almost 30 years ( AFP/Getty )

Taoiseach Micheál Martin also voiced deep concern over the unfolding standoff while appealing for calm.

Mr Martin criticized the Parades Commission’s ruling to permit the march down Garvaghy Road for the first time in nearly 30 years as "incomprehensible and wrong".

The legal clearance allowing the parade to proceed was finalized at 2.15am on Sunday following lengthy arguments presented by opposing legal teams.

The overnight hearing formed part of three distinct emergency legal actions brought before Belfast courts between Saturday and Sunday morning.

Justice Michael Humphreys presided over the final time-sensitive session, which opened at 12.20am on Sunday.

In his opening remarks, he highlighted the "unusual if not unprecedented circumstances as it is now 1.45am, with a parade scheduled to begin in just over six hours’ time".

In delivering his ruling, Justice Humphreys emphasized legal precedent requiring courts to respect decisions by public bodies, noting "their decisions will not be lightly interfered with".

He remarked: "The picture painted here is of a public body which took evidence from the relevant sources, weighed up the key issues which were in play and arrived at a reasoned decision.

"The jurisdiction to impugn (a) public body’s decision on that basis is necessarily limited to cases where no reasonable decision could arrive at that outcome and in my view, in this case that threshold has not been met."

He further noted: "This court cannot substitute its own view or anyone else’s view for that of the commission."

Earlier, Lady Chief Justice Siobhan Keegan, Northern Ireland’s senior judge, similarly described the situation as "unprecedented" while hearing the second legal challenge.

Justices Keegan and Humphreys sat alongside Lady Justice Denise McBride in the Court of Appeal late on Saturday to grant an appeal brought by Portadown Orangeman Alan Hynes, permitting the march. That decision overturned a temporary injunction granted earlier on Saturday that would have halted the procession.

In that initial ruling, Justice Patricia Smyth suspended the commission’s permission, warning that the "long-running dispute has the potential to escalate" throughout the region.

Tensions surrounding Drumcree gained national attention throughout the 1990s as nationalist residents on Garvaghy Road opposed the parade passing through their neighborhood, prompting repeated summer clashes and extensive police operations.

For over twenty-five years, the Orange Order has repeatedly sought permission to finish the route it was blocked from completing in 1998.

On Friday, the commission overturned its established position, drawing support from unionist politicians alongside sharp criticism from nationalist and republican representatives.

The approval permitted the march under strict conditions, restricting participation to 35 individuals and maintaining the 8am start time.

News.title: Five reasons why Australia’s win over Boks was an all-time classic
News.content:
If the Wallabies play like this in their own backyard at their own World Cup next year, boy we are in for a treat. After years in the doldrums, this five-try victory over South Africa was the latest reminder of their transformation under the stewardship of Les Kiss.

Their gritty performance in Perth – the city where Australia will open rugby’s showpiece in 12 months’ time – was caveated by the fact they were facing a second-string Boks side. But there can be no denying they are on an upward trajectory, even if their discipline dramatically deserted them late on.

In a helter-skelter denouement, Australia played the majority of the final 10 minutes of the match with 11 men on the pitch as South Africa threatened to mount a late comeback. Tom Wright’s eye-catching intercept try looked to have secured a match-winning moment, but it was scratched off after Hunter Paisami joined Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan and Joseph Sua’ali’i in the bin.

Ox Nche’s 80th-minute score made it a four-point game with time left for the restart, but Australia had enough fight to secure a dramatic victory largely built on execution and patience.

Five tries by the hour mark, including a Len Ikitau first-half double, ultimately gave South Africa a mountain to climb. The Wallabies’ field coverage and industriousness in defence was far superior to that of the four-time world champions, while Max Jorgensen and Sua’ali’i were pillars of excellence out wide.

After clinching a 3-1 win over New Zealand in their historic “Greatest Rivalry” series, Rassie Erasmus had the luxury of resting several of his A-listers for this one-off Test in Western Australia. The changes ultimately had an adverse effect, with the visitors faulty at the set-piece and lacking their usual snarl and bite. They found themselves playing catch-up in a chaotic game that Australia, despite their discipline creaking in the dying moments, deserved to win.

Here, Telegraph Sport explores five reasons why this was one of the craziest Test matches in recent memory.

Wallabies outmuscle Boks over 60 emphatic minutes

The Wallabies front up impressively to earn a seven-point lead at the break after a quickfire Len Ikitau double cancels out tries from Johan Grobbelaar and Edwill van der Merwe, before Ben Donaldson finishes a sublime attacking set from the hosts.

News.title: England show ODI depth in thrashing of Sri Lanka
News.content:
England’s international summer comes to an end at the Oval with a series decider against Sri Lanka. After England won the first game in Durham, Sri Lanka bounced back to take a 16-run win at Headingley on Thursday to set up this winner-takes-all match today. Sri Lanka put up a much better fight in the second one-day international than they have throughout the rest of their white-ball tour. The tourists posted 321 for six, with their captain Kusal Mendis leading the way with 121 off 100 balls, his seventh ODI century.

England’s reply got off to the best possible start, with both openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett hitting fifties. It appeared to be going well for England, with Jos Buttler and Will Jacks also registering half centuries, but Buttler’s hamstring injury in addition to the regular loss of wickets meant Sri Lanka were able to claim victory to take us to a series decider in London today.

“I am so happy winning and getting the hundred,” Mendis said. “The overall performance was very good. We started really well and the middle order batted really well. Nothing special, basic cricket and I was very happy with 320, we wanted more than 300 on this pitch. [Dunith] Wellalage bowled really well, the whole team, after the powerplay. The guys gave 100 per cent. Today [Thursday] is finished and now we have to focus on the next game and do the basics right.”

When Buttler retired hurt in the 38th over of England’s run chase, the hosts were 254 for four and were in a great position to chase the total down and claim a series victory. From the 37th over onwards, England were only able to score one four and one six.

“It was an outstanding game,” England captain Harry Brook said. “You can look back and dwell on some many different areas but that is not what this team does, we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the Oval. We put up a really good fight with the ball. To restrict them to 320 and have the chance to chase that down was a hell of an effort.

“The lads got the chase off to a flyer. You could not really ask for much more. We probably stalled in that middle period and lost a few too many wickets, but the fight we showed was great. We have got a great opportunity now to try and win this series, and a great opportunity for 12 months’ time. In pressure situations, like the one that awaits us at the Oval, it will be great to see where we are as a team.”

Buttler has been ruled out of this match due to a hamstring injury and has been replaced in the squad by Dan Lawrence, who had been playing for Surrey in the final round of the County Championship.

Play from the Oval will get under way at 10.30am.

News.title: Saracens storm Leicester to launch new Venter era in style
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Gallagher Prem meeting as Leicester Tigers host Saracens at Welford Road.

Last season, Leicester reached the play-off semi-finals in Geoff Parling’s first full season at the club, before losing to arch-rivals Northampton Saints, who went on to win their third title in the competition.

In a new era for Leicester as they plot a route back to the very top, Aaron Wainwright and Mako Vunipola make their Prem debuts.

Leicester head coach Geoff Parling is brimming with excitement ahead of this tasty match and has talked about his side’s preparation for the new season.

“Firstly we are looking to evolve our game, we’re not looking to rip it up and completely restart,” he said. This team is built on being competitive and winning, we’ve got to be in the mix every year. For me it’s all about being consistently near the top and then getting in those big games and having the ability to perform in them.”

“I’m well aware that there’s lots of elements from the season and different circumstances but the main thing is that the league is designed to have a top four that go into the play-offs so the top four is the aim.”

Saracens finished one place below Leicester in the previous campaign and missed out on the play-offs after a 32-12 final round loss to Exeter Chiefs.

Boss Joe Shaw has handed debuts to Tomos Williams and Alfie Barbeary, and he’s raring to go ahead of this fixture.

“We’ve had a great pre-season, but we’re itching to get stuck into the league campaign now,” he said. “We have a really competitive squad who are driving standards and good habits across the pitch. We are confident in the squad we have put together and are excited to see what they can achieve this campaign.”

Kick-off is at 15:00.

News.title: England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation
News.content:
Tuchel does not plan to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”

News.title: Red Roses triumph over New Zealand in chaotic late scenes – how it unfolded
News.content:
Just when it looked like the Red Roses’ lustre was beginning to fade, up stepped Zoe Harrison.

In one of the most dramatic finishes to an England match in recent memory, the fly-half gobbled up Amy Du Plessis’s pass to glide over the whitewash and secure a pulsating win over New Zealand.

Ever the epitome of calmness, Harrison was undeterred by the fact she had just missed what would have been a match-winning penalty from 42 metres out with the score locked at 19-19.

But after their arm-wrestle with Canada last weekend in Exeter, which finished 26-26, there was simply no way the Red Roses were going to settle for a draw for a second week running.

A year to the day since they were crowned world champions in their own back yard, England’s status as the most dominant side in the women’s game was all but confirmed by this never-say-die victory over the Black Ferns.

News.title: Russell holds his nerve to see off Verstappen and win Azerbaijan GP
News.content:
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend went the way many believed the 2026 season would play out. George Russell strolled to victory from pole, though with a little late jeopardy, whilst Kimi Antonelli’s crash in qualifying meant he had to fight his way through the field to finish fifth. That, after all, was the order of things last season.

Yet the past few days in Baku are an inversion of the season’s storyline. It is Antonelli who has been the faster driver, heading for a maiden world title at the second time of asking. Russell has been the troubled one. This was only the Briton’s third victory of the season and his first since Austria in late June. Antonelli has racked up eight wins and, before this weekend in Baku, a well-deserved 81-point lead over Russell.

Russell’s dominant and impressive run from pole to the chequered flag on Saturday is both a reminder of what he is capable of and also what might have been, had he been able to find this type of form earlier and more often. The reality, though, is that he needs to replicate this for the rest of the season to even be in with a sniff, barring a catastrophic meltdown from Antonelli. Still, Russell looked elated to have ended his barren run.

The finish was a little more tense than Russell deserved, having established a healthy lead in the first half of the race. Two late safety cars eradicated his advantage and helped put Max Verstappen’s Red Bull on his gearbox. In the end, he triumphed by just under 0.2sec and, as Antonelli finished fifth – with some help from two safety-car inducing crashes – he made up 15 points on his Mercedes team-mate. Isack Hadjar completed the podium for Red Bull after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.

News.title: Scotland’s Pocognoli era starts with encouraging signs but familiar issues in front of goal
News.content:
Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

News.title: Carreras’ try-of-season contender helps Bath eclipse Harlequins
News.content:
And they kept playing, it was not until Richards scored in the 72nd minute that the game was decided. Still for Bath, a five-try victory away from home, felt like a decent return.

If they were to stand any chance of finding a way back into the game, Quins had to score first after the restart. They were rewarded for their attacking intent after running from a scrum deep in their half, with Murley cutting a brilliant line before Pedro Delgado drove over for his side’s third try.

Quins had the opportunity to further cut the deficit when first Sam Riley carried down the left wing and Cameron Anderson drove into the Bath 22. But as Quins looked to pick and go, Beno Obano and Guy Pepper combined to hold the ball up over the line.

It felt like a significant moment and when Riley was shown a yellow card for a high tackle on Obano moments later, the odds against a Quins comeback lengthened again. Yet there was something sticky about their resilience.

“I am really happy with the grit and the fight that they showed, particularly in the second half,” said Gilmore. “We had some massive defensive sets on our goal-line which we withstood. I reckon they were the moments last year that Bath would probably run in three tries really quickly and kick the score out, which is good.”

Bath emptied their bench, including the introduction of England flanker Pepper, but they could not pull away as expected in the final quarter, despite some impressive contributions by Tom de Glanville.

It was left to their line-out maul to score their first points of the second half, with Richards touching down to seal Harlequins’ fate. Still, there were enough promising glimpses to give Harlequins supporters hope that more encouraging days lie ahead.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick has to use what happened to him vs Man City as turning point at Manchester United
Sports.content:
Next

THE BALL got rolling for Manchester City’s period of ‘dominance’ when Michael Carrick rolled the ball into the path of Yaya Toure in 2011.

Carrick’s errant pass in the FA Cup semi-final was intercepted by the City midfielder, who charged into the area and slotted past Edwin van der Sar for the Wembley winner.



To put it into context, that April day was City’s first at Wembley since the 1999 Division 2 Play-off final against Gillingham, staged four days after United clinched the treble in Barcelona.

It was a repeat in the 2011 against Stoke final: 1-0 to City, goalscorer Toure. That ended City’s 35-year wait for silverware.



The ticker banner affixed to Old Trafford’s Stretford End had to be taken down. On Friday night, an image of the banner circulated among United fans on WhatsApp. It read “50 years”.

Toure’s goal is totally tainted now, as are the eight Premier League titles, four FA Cups, seven League Cups, European Cup and Club World Cup City have since chiselled on to their honours’ board. It is a roll of dishonour.

City have commissioned a few documentaries in the past ten years. The streaming sites may now have to begin with a disclaimer akin to ones that warn viewers about strobe lighting or outdated cultural depictions in classic films.

“The following events happened, but are rendered hollow and meaningless by the club’s financial chicanery” may suffice.

The revelation that City have been found guilty of the majority of the Premier League’s 115 charges does not change how United players felt at full-time 15-and-a-half years ago.

Paul Scholes took out his frustration with a crude foul on Pablo Zabaleta and was sent off. Rio Ferdinand and Anderson confronted a mischievous Mario Balotelli at full-time.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Tellingly, there is no mention of Toure in Carrick’s 2018 book. Toure is a fellow midfielder whom Carrick played against in a Champions League final and countless Manchester derbies.

An entire chapter is simply titled ‘Rome’, dedicated to the 2009 Champions League final debacle against Barcelona. Toure, admittedly, filled in at centre back to offset the suspensions of Dani Alves and Eric Abidal.

Sir Alex Ferguson dropped Carrick after high-profile errors against Burnley and Bayern Munich in 2009-10. The latter is covered in chapter and verse in Carrick’s autobiography, as he revealed that Ferguson barely spoke to him in the final weeks of that season.

Ferguson was more forgiving of Carrick’s Wembley lapse. He lined up at Newcastle three days later. But it is striking that the 2011 semi does not merit a single mention in Carrick’s written reflections of his playing career.

At Carrington in 11 days, he will be peppered with questions about Friday’s seismic news. It is good news for Carrick on two fronts. His final campaign as a player was 2017-18 when United came second to centurions City. He may retrospectively receive a winner’s medal.



The inordinate international break reduced the heat on Carrick and now it is off him. United still have a fortnight to wait until they next play again against Tottenham.

Carrick likes to hold press conferences two days before matchday and the schedule affords him that. He has to use it as a reset.

In recent weeks, he has seldom sounded or acted like a United manager. That has to change if United are to resist changing manager.



Carrick was more bullish at his last pre-match sit down. He engaged in a back-and-forth with a journalist who questioned him on an apparent lack of passion and branded it “ridiculous” to wonder how long he would remain in charge.

Tub-thumping is not Carrick’s style but sitting on the fence will not suffice. He did not go for the throat in the derby when City were reduced to ten men but has another chance now.

The memory of Toure leaving Carrick in his wake and Enzo Maresca skipping down the touchline upon confirmation Erling Haaland’s illegitimate goal would stand should stir Carrick. Maresca did not shake hands at full-time, either.

Carrick confronted City goalkeeper Ederson after the December 2017 derby amid their dressing room celebrations. Carrick’s only career red card was for kicking a ball away accidentally, so it is not in his nature to be confrontational but he is well within his rights to cut City down to size.

When Carrick took his son, Jacey, to watch United at Burnley in January 2018, the away-dayers urged him to give them a song. Carrick belted out “U-N-I-T-E-D”. The lyrics end with “Why don’t City f**k off home”.



Jose Mourinho could not resist aiming a barb at City on the eve of his reunion with United as Fenerbahce manager in October 2024.

“We finished second in the Premier League,” Mourinho said in Istanbul. “I think we still have a chance to win that league because maybe they punish Man City with points.

“And maybe we win that league and they have to pay me the bonus and give me the medal!”

RECOMMENDED STORIES



During Carrick’s final season, Mourinho privately complained his United were competing against a “state”.

City are in a state now.

Sports.title: Ireland players snub Israel handshakes and take action during national anthem before match
Sports.content:
Ireland players snub Israel handshakes and take action during national anthem before match

The Republic of Ireland faced Israel in the Nations League on Sunday evening, making a number of demonstrations ahead of kick-off due to the ongoing conflict in Gaza

View 2 Images Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the Israeli national anthem (Image: Attila KISBENEDEK / AFP via Getty Images)

Republic of Ireland players snubbed shaking hands with their Israeli opponents during Sunday evening's Nations League clash at the Nagyerdei Stadion. Heimir Hallgrimsson's men also bowed their heads during Israel's national anthem.

‌



It was a tense state of affairs as both sets of players made their way onto the pitch for the encounter, with no exchange of pennants. Captains, Dara O'Shea and Manor Solomon, also did not shake hands before or after the referee's coin toss to delegate kick-off and pitch sides.

‌



Ireland also made the decision to wear black armbands for the encounter, in recognition of the lives lost in the Gaza conflict. It comes as there were questions asked with regard to whether the match should have taken place at all, considering Israel's ongoing war with Palestine.

‌



Football Association of Ireland chief, David Courell told the press earlier this week that players held an intra-squad vote regarding their participation in the match against Israel, with a majority opting to go ahead. However, Gavin Bazunu withdrew himself from Hallgrimsson's squad on account of personal beliefs.

Ireland forced into unusual decision after squad split over controversial Israel match READ MORE :

Why Ireland players are wearing black armbands against Israel after player vote READ MORE :

Taking to Instagram, the Bolton Wanderers goalkeeper wrote: "My decision is based purely upon my personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong," adding: "It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition of the Israeli people or the Jewish community but against the atrocities in the region."

As a result of UEFA regulations for the competition, which stipulate that each squad must register at least three goalkeepers, Ireland made the decision to call up defender Jimmy Dunne to theoretically play backup to Caoimhin Kelleher and Max O'Leary - although the likelihood of him actually taking up a role in net is slim to none.

‌



Speaking about Ireland's decision to play Israel, Courell said: "The squad were in Pristina yesterday. An extensive conversation took place where ultimately the consensus from the group was to travel to Hungary.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 2 Images Gavin Bazunu pulled out of the fixture

‌



"That was something that we all entered into this window with our intention to fulfil these fixtures and that was the consensus that the group finished on at the end of that two-hour meeting yesterday. This morning a player (now confirmed to be Bazunu) expressed their discomfort with fulfilling this fixture to the head coach and indicated their intent to withdraw from the squad.

"As you can understand, this new variable required time and deliberation for the rest of the squad to consider. What proceeded was another four hours of conversations, predominantly amongst the players themselves but also at times with the coaching staff and at times with the executive.

"There was a lot of positions presented and I think it's important to say that from an association perspective and for everyone involved in those conversations, we were fully respectful of everyone's right to their respective opinion on these topics.

Article continues below

"Ultimately within the last maybe 90 minutes we carried out a vote amongst the squad to establish their sentiment on fulfilling the fixtures and it was a significant majority that was returned with the intention to continue."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel on collision course with Premier League bosses after blunt refusal
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel on collision course with Premier League bosses after blunt refusal

England players face a gruelling four games in 11 days, but Thomas Tuchel is adamant he will not listen to Premier League managers who ask for their stars to be rested

View 3 Images England manager Thomas Tuchel will not rest players during the international break (Image: Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel will refuse to take any calls from Premier League managers - and insists it would be “madness” to expect him to rest players.

‌



Tuchel is ready to put himself on collision course with club bosses over England’s Nations League schedule as they face four games in the space of 11 days.

‌



England’s top stars came back from the World Cup exhausted, had short summer holidays and are straight back into a grueling fixture list with their clubs.

‌



But Tuchel insists he is determined to pick his strongest XI throughout the course of this international window even if Premier League clubs will be anxious about players getting injuries.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



England go straight from playing Spain at Wembley on Saturday to facing Czech Republic on Tuesday, Croatia next Saturday and then Czech Republic again at Wembley on Tuesday October 6.

England boss Tuchel said: “I don’t take calls from Premier League managers. I never called any national team coach. It is what it is.

“I cannot manage the players. It’s just impossible. I knew as a club coach – when I was on the other side – that I had this example many times.

‌



“If I would call a coach in Brazil or Argentina, they would not know what I am talking about. The players would not know what I am talking about.

View 3 Images England will play four games in 11 days

“So why would I do this and start giving the players the impression that it’s okay to take a step back or share a half or to rest one match? Why would I? I would never. It’s madness. We want to win the next match.”

‌



England had mass withdrawals before the squad met up with Declan Rice - who came to Wembley to support his England teammates - Cole Palmer, Tino Livramento, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo all pulling out.

Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner were called up and Tuchel does expect to make some changes through the run of fixtures but he will keep the core of the team which narrowly lost to Spain together.

Tuchel says that is his “ideal scenario” and has also suggested players may have to be subbed off early before getting into the dangerous territory when they are tired and fatigued at the end of games.

‌



View 3 Images England started their Nations League campaign with defeat to Spain

But Tuchel says he plans to play high intensity football against the Czech Republic - and there will be no let up in his demands.

Tuchel added: “Hopefully we can find that kind of shape and form but if you mean like ‘do we go for it and try to impose what we did today’ then yes that’s 100 per cent.

Article continues below

“We need to be proactive and go for it. There is no room for managing or an economic style. It’s how the team want to play, how we want to play so let’s go. It will be a different scenario and setting and a different challenge.”

Sports.title: Man Utd dealt second injury blow as star limps off after Bruno Fernandes issue
Sports.content:
Man Utd dealt second injury blow as star limps off after Bruno Fernandes issue

Manchester United have been hit with further injury concerns just days after Bruno Fernandes suffered a 'complicated problem' against Wales in the Nations League

View 2 Images Patrick Dorgu limped off the pitch against Wales

Patrick Dorgu was forced off the pitch during Denmark's Nations League clash with Wales on Sunday afternoon, sparking further injury worries for Manchester United. It comes after Bruno Fernandes found himself injured against the same nation while representing Portugal.

‌



While Dorgu was selected to start on the left wing by Danish head coach, Brian Riemer, the 21-year-old lasted just 30 minutes of the encounter with the Red Dragons. The Red Devils talent was spotted falling to the turf in frustration before holding his leg, with Mohamed Daramy called upon to take his place.

‌



Dorgu was also spotted limping as he made his way off the pitch, in what could be a cause for concern regarding not only Denmark - who have another two matches to play this international break - but also United. He is the second United player who has taken a knock during the current Premier League break.

‌



Club captain, Fernandes, has joined Portugal on international duty, with his nation facing Wales earlier this week - running out 1-0 winners thanks to an early strike from Joao Felix. However, having picked up an injury during that encounter, he is now expected to miss Portugal's game with Norway on Sunday evening.

Bruno Fernandes cut from Portugal squad due to UEFA rules and 'complicated' issue READ MORE :

Premier League clubs consider legal action as Man Utd react to Man City guilty verdict READ MORE :

Head coach, Jorge Jesus, described the injury as a "complicated problem" when addressing the media in the aftermath of Portugal's Nations League opener. He said: "In the game against Wales, we went in with all the available players but Bruno Fernandes came off with a complicated problem."

He added: "He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United. He really wanted to play against Wales. He wasn’t at his usual level, we’ll see if he’s ready."

‌



Jesus continued: "He said he’s been dealing with that pain for about three games, and that was one of the factors that prevented him from being at his usual level against Wales.

"He was my player, I know him perfectly. I’ve already spoken to him. I prefer not to risk him in this game and have him clean and in good physical condition for the Denmark game."

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes is also carrying an injury (Image: Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Carrick will be hopeful that the injuries that Dorgu and Fernandes are currently carrying will have dissipated by the time they return to club football in a little under two weeks' time, considering United's current medical list.

Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo made the decision to snub England call-ups from Thomas Tuchel to prioritise their respective recoveries from minor knocks, while Benjamin Sesko also ruled himself out of representing Slovenia as a result of a leg problem.

Article continues below

Matthijs de Ligt has not represented the Red Devils since last November, owing to a back injury, while Manuel Ugarte is another long-term absentee through a knee injury sustained this summer. Tom Heaton, Karl Darlow and Amad Diallo are also sidelined at the moment.

Sports.title: Referee calls half-time two minutes early before U-turn after furious player backlash
Sports.content:
Referee calls half-time two minutes early before U-turn after furious player backlash

Players from both teams surrounded the referee after being short changed two first-half minutes and their furious backlash eventually led to a U-turn being made

View 2 Images Several players surrounded Isaac Searle after the first half's early end (Image: Sky Sports)

English Football League (EFL) referee Isaac Searle blew his whistle for half-time two minutes early during the League Two match between Oldham Athletic and Salford City. Only two of the four minutes of additional time had been played at Boundary Park when Mathew Hudson launched a long goal kick up-field.

‌



Searle then called time after the ball crossed in Salford's half just seconds into the 48th minute. Players from both sides, particularly from Oldham, who were 2-1 behind at the time, immediately complained.

‌



After a minute of deliberation, play eventually resumed. Searle had to beckon players who had left the pitch back on.

‌



Commentating on the match for Sky Sports, Joe Shennan: "That is, perhaps a little earlier than expected, the end of the first half. And Oldham are furious here with Isaac Searle."

Ireland forced into unusual decision after squad split over controversial Israel match READ MORE :

Oldham's Jamie Robson bounded over to the referee before shouting an arm's length away from his face. Keenan Appiah-Forson was already on the scene holding up four fingers, a gesture that Mike Fondop made after getting in between Robson and Searle.

Salford pair Brendan Wiredu and Will Aimison were also in the vicinity before eventually departing. The hosts' goalkeeper coach, Scott Davies, also came on the field to remonstrate.

‌



Shennan continued: "Two and a half minutes through four added at the end of the first half, and it appears as though we have reached the break. Oldham cannot contain their fury; they are behind.

"And what is the referee going to say here? Is he gonna call both sets of players back out, perhaps?

View 2 Images It took around a minute before Isaac Searle waved players back onto the pitch (Image: Sky Sports)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Well, this is something that you don't often see anywhere in the EFL. They were ready for the half-time entertainment, but there is confusion in the stands and on the touchline." Television footage showed Oldham staff carrying two sets of goals back off the pitch.

One of Searle's assistant referees came across to consult with his colleague. So, too, did fourth official Sebastian Stockbridge.

Article continues below

After speaking to the latter, players were waved back onto the pitch, with the majority having walked off. Play restarted from the goal-kick, and they played out the remaining 90 seconds without further incident.

Co-commentator Sue Smith said: "Well, I've never seen anything like it, Joe. Certainly, a misunderstanding wasn't there? "I think some of the players have gone and had their drinks, and they were all ready to have a little half-time break, but I thought, 'it's way too early'.

Sports.title: Alexander Isak injury explained as boss provides update on Liverpool star
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak injury explained as boss provides update on Liverpool star

Alexander Isak will return to Liverpool after his injury against Romania proved to be worse than first thought, leaving Sweden without him for rest of their September-October internationals

View 2 Images Alexander Isak has left the Sweden squad (Image: Jonathan Nackstrand/AFP via Getty Images)

Sweden boss Graham Potter has provided an update on Alexander Isak, revealing that the Liverpool star has suffered a thigh injury. Isak, 27, withdrew from international duty on the eve of Monday's game against Poland, with Liverpool confirming that he'll return to the club for treatment.

‌



Although the striker was spotted with a bloodied toe after scoring in Friday's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League, Potter has clarified that Isak was actually forced to withdraw because of a thigh problem. The injury will see him miss Sweden's remaining three matches during the international window.

‌



"He's got a small problem with his thigh," Potter explained at his pre-match press conference. "It's not a big one but because of the amount of games we've got in a small space of time, he won't be able to make those.

‌



"Not a big one but it's frustrating for him and obviously for us. It is what it is but we move forward with the players we have.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"It was during the game. Like anything, you sometimes get bumps and bruises in the game, you might think it's a bit of a dead leg or something. But actually as the 24 hours, 48 hours after the game, not quite what you think.

"Unfortunately after getting it checked out, it's a little bit more than what you think during the match. He has to miss the rest of the camp.

"Our medical team has been in contact with the club. Obviously it's our decision in the first place because of his status, in terms of his injury. Once that's the case, we have to inform everybody. That's just normal.

‌



Who has been Liverpool's player of the season so far? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Graham Potter admits that no one can replace Alexander Isak (Image: Jonathan Nackstrand/AFP via Getty Images)

"We've got a really big squad that we believe in. Clearly there's not another Alexander Isak, that's obvious.

‌



"In an ideal world, we want all our players available but the reality is we don't have Alex for this game… clearly whoever comes in, we're not going to ask them to be Alex. They just need to be themselves in the best way they can."

Sweden are top of League B Group 4 after beating Romania on home soil. Potter's side welcome Poland to Stockholm in a repeat of March's World Cup play-off final which Sweden won 3-2 thanks to a late goal from Viktor Gyokeres.

As for Isak, his focus will be on ensuring that he's available for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City on October 11. Three days later, the Reds travel to Austria to face LASK in the Champions League as part of a run of nine games in 27 days.

Sports.title: Scottish football match ends 14-0 as manager speaks out on 'bizarre' situation
Sports.content:
Scottish football match ends 14-0 as manager speaks out on 'bizarre' situation

The Scottish Challenge Cup played out in remarkable fashion this weekend, with one team running out to a 14-0 victory in ruthless fashion

View 2 Images Ross County ran out 14-0 winners over Hearts B in the Scottish Challenge Cup (Image: Daily Record)

Ross County broke a 33-year-old club record on Saturday, as they demolished Hearts II in a 14-0 win in the KDM Evolution Trophy. The Young Jambos saw six put past them in the first-half, with a Robbie Flockhart red card opening the doors for further embarrassment.

‌



Kieran Phillips managed a quartet of goals in the first 45, with Ricco Diack also bagging a brace before the half-time break. On the other side of the interval, Phillips bolstered his tally to five, while Diack completed his hat-trick from the penalty spot.

‌



Chris Hamilton also managed three of his own in the second-half, while Luke McCarvel found the back of the net twice. Jamie Lindsay's solitary strike made the overall score 14-0 in a day to quickly forget for Hearts' B side.

‌



It came as County's fourth win of the KDM Evolution Trophy, skyrocketing them to second in the league standings. At the time of writing, the club trail Clydebank by just a single point, with a goal difference of +22.

Thomas Tuchel has failed his main England task and Spain defeat felt inevitable READ MORE :

Liverpool confirm Alexander Isak injury status after star returns from Sweden duty READ MORE :

However, they also broke a 33-year club record in the process of their hellish 14-0 win over Hearts' B team. That's because until Saturday, the club's highest win had came in the form of an 11-0 win over St Cuthberts Wanderers in 1993.

Should Ross County have any hopes of breaking the overall record for the highest margin of victory, however, they still have work to do. That's because Abroath managed a staggering 36-0 win ove Shotts Bon Accord back in 1885.

‌



Up next for County in the Scottish Challenge Cup in a final league phase fixture with Forfar Athletic come Tuesday, October 13.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

And while many a head coach will have been elated with Saturday's win, Stuart Kettlewell didn't let the scoreline get to his head.

‌



Speaking in the aftermath of the match, he said: "I think my biggest focus, as always, is my team. I think that they treated the game exactly how it should be treated.

"Fully professional performance. Obviously, it seems a bit bizarre at the number of goals that were scored in the game.

View 2 Images Stuart Kettlewell was understandably happy with his club's performance (Image: YouTube / Ross County)

‌



"The fact that Hearts go down to 10 men, I think it was at four at the time, they just continued to do what I asked them to do, which is play the game at fast pace, play to go and score goals, play to go and get the ball into wide areas to look to get crosses in.

"There was a lot of good quality from within the game, of course, from our side. But as I say, my focus goes onto our team. If we come here and start stroking the ball about and killing a bit of time, and wasting people's time here today that have come to try and see us score some goals and win a game of football, then I think, again, we're kidding people on.

"So the players have approached that absolutely how I wanted them to do so. But I can't say I'm surprised, because I feel like I'm saying that to you almost every single week.

Article continues below

"In terms of what it means for the competition, it's another win, another three points on the board for us. And significant confidence, it would have to be said, towards a lot of individuals in our team, to be able to get onto the scoresheet and to be able to perform well, yet again."

Sports.title: Erling Haaland's dad admitted his son could leave Man City and named six clubs he could join
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's dad admitted his son could leave Man City and named six clubs he could join

Erling Haaland signed a nine-and-a-half-year contract with Manchester City, but his dad believes he could be on the move soon

View 2 Images Erling Haaland's dad believes his son could leave Manchester City (Image: Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images)

Alf-Inge Haaland once claimed his son won't be at Manchester City forever - and could even leave at the end of this season. The ex-Premier League star named several clubs his son could join in the future, including Barcelona, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



Haaland Sr's words have resurfaced after City were found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges they faced for financial rule breaches. The club could face points deductions, be stripped of trophies and even be relegated to the lower leagues.

‌



Haaland was slated to speak ahead of Norway's clash with Portugal, but was removed from media duties. TV2 reported that the striker has been replaced by Benfica duo Andreas Schjelderup and Fredrik Aursnes.

‌



Long before the news broke about City's charges, Haaland Sr addressed his son's potential career and admitted he expects him to compete in all the top leagues around the world. In 2022, the ex-Leeds man appeared on the documentary, Haaland: The Big Decision, and was frank about what he believes will happen.

Premier League bosses urged to immediately RELEGATE Man City after 115 charges verdict READ MORE :

The 53-year-old said: "I think Erling wants to prove his abilities in all leagues. Then he can stay there [Manchester City] for three or four years at the most. He could be, for example, two-and-a-half years in Germany, two-and-a-half years in England and then in Spain, Italy, France, right?"

With the time frame in mind, Haaland Sr believes his son could depart at the end of the current season. The ex-striker even had some clubs in mind, naming six that he thought the Norway international could consider.

‌



He added: "On our list, I think City is the best team. [Bayern] Munich is number two. We have Real Madrid as number three, Paris Saint-Germain as number four.

View 2 Images Haaland could consider leaving City (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

"We also have some English teams other than City who are quite good. Liverpool and Chelsea. Also, there is Barcelona. They are sort of in the same row."

‌



In 2025, Haaland signed a contract extension that ties him to City until 2034. However, Real and Barcelona have both previously eyed the striker and may see the charges as a new incentive to secure his services.

The 26-year-old is yet to address City's verdict, but previously claimed he wants to remain at the club for a long time. Discussing his bumper new contract last year, Haaland said: "It has been amazing, and it's been like a dream these past two and a half years, but I'm really looking forward to what's next and for the future.

"I'm going to stay for a long time so now I can fully focus on getting better because [I know] I'm going to stay for such a long time. So, [the] full focus [is] on performing and getting better and to give all the fans what they want."

Sports.title: Liverpool confirm Alexander Isak injury status after star returns from Sweden duty
Sports.content:
Liverpool confirm Alexander Isak injury status after star returns from Sweden duty

Liverpool striker Alexander Isak scored in Sweden's Nations League victory over Romania but will now return to Anfield earlier than planned after suffering a knock

View 2 Images Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool (Image: Patrick Smith/FIFA)

Liverpool have announced that Alexander Isak has returned early from international duty after sustaining a 'minor injury' during a Sweden game.

‌



The Reds striker scored in a 2-1 win for Graham Potter's team over Romania to continue his prolific start to the season. However, Isak's evening was marred by a stamp which left him with a bloody toe, although he played down the severity of the issue during a post-match conversation with the media.

‌



"You can see it [the injury], "Isak is said to have told reporters. "It was a real stamp. Those of you who have played might know that it takes a few minutes before it lets go, but it was okay."

‌



Though Isak did not seem concerned, it has now been confirmed by Liverpool that he will no longer participate in Sweden's remaining three fixtures during the international break, with Potter later confirming the 27-year-old had a thigh issue.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"Alexander Isak is to return to Liverpool from international duty due to a minor injury," a Liverpool statement read.

"The striker will not be involved in Sweden’s three remaining fixtures in the current international break and will now be assessed by club medical staff at the AXA Training Centre."

After enduring a challenging maiden campaign at Anfield, Isak has finally started to show glimpses of a return to form in the opening weeks of the 2026-27 campaign, scoring four Premier League goals in five games for Liverpool.

‌



That return is already better than Isak's goal tally for last season - but Andoni Iraola wants even more following his return to form.

View 2 Images Isak has started the season in fine form for club and country (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

Speaking after Isak plundered the winner against Bournemouth prior to the break, Iraola called for the striker to be more involved in play, saying: “He took the chance after a quiet afternoon – and that’s what a striker’s job is like.

‌



“He had a couple of situations, a cross he didn’t hit properly, one when his control wasn’t right and then the goal.

“But he has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition half and to have meaningful possession.

“Then, if the team is playing there, he will receive the rewards in terms of goals. We need that level so that we can play better.”

Sports.title: Kohli passes 15,000 ODI runs as hundred helps India beat West Indies
Sports.content:
Virat Kohli celebrated his return to the international arena by hitting his 55th ODI hundred as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in the series opener on Sunday.

India's star batter - who now only plays this format in international cricket - smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, including 10 fours and nine sixes, as India successfully chased down 296 in just 41.4 overs.

In doing so, the 37-year-old also became only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar (18,426) to pass 15,000 runs in ODIs.

"My focus has never been on milestones. Just looking back at the start of my journey, it makes me feel very grateful," Kohli said. "I enjoy each and every minute that I am out there playing for India, and I am able to do the job for my team. As a cricketer, this is all I could dream of."

Skipper Shubman Gill also notched a century, scoring 110 off 108 deliveries as India registered an easy win - clinched with a Kohli six - to go 1-0 up in the three-match series.

Earlier, West Indies had posted 295-7 from their 50 overs after being put into bat. Opener Justin Greaves (101 off 108) scored his maiden ODI ton, sharing in an impressive 135-run opening partnership with John Campbell (62 off 60) inside the first 20 overs.

Wrist spinner Kuldeep Yadav (4-40) ultimately accounted for both as he wreaked havoc in the middle overs to see West Indies reduced to 198-5 by the 36th.

Amir Jangoo's unbeaten 58 off 43 balls helped revive the innings, but their target of 296 ultimately proved an under-par one on a batter-friendly pitch.

It was a quick-fire chase for India as openers Gill and Rohit Sharma added 74 off 72 balls, Sharma scoring 32 off 35 before he fell to Alzarri Joseph (1-81) in the 12th over.

Kohli came to the crease and promptly eased his way to fifty in only 40 balls, hitting the 15,000-milestone on the way - the fastest to do it at 303 innings, compared to Tendulkar's 377.

He and Gill put on 151 off 132 balls for the second wicket before the captain departed against the run of play to Roston Chase (1-64) in the 34th over.

But Kohli cruised to a 74-ball hundred, before finishing the game in style with 8.2 overs to spare. Kohli's nine sixes were his most in an ODI innings.

Guwahati and Chandigarh will host the second and third ODIs on Wednesday and Saturday, followed by a five-match T20 series starting on October 6.

Sports.title: Thompson strike seals Chelsea win to end Arsenal's unbeaten run
Sports.content:
Alyssa Thompson scored the only goal as Chelsea secured a 1-0 win against Arsenal to end their unbeaten streak in the Women's Super League.

Arsenal failed to make their early dominance count after striking the post twice through Kim Little and Mariona Caldentey before Thompson broke the deadlock at Stamford Bridge.

Keira Walsh's strike from distance was initially well kept out by Anneke Borbe, but the goalkeeper was left helpless when Thompson pounced in the box to fire home the rebound in emphatic style.

The Gunners - who had drawn their last two WSL matches - improved in the second half, with Chloe Kelly's angled drive blocked and Alessia Russo's shot charged down, but the hosts saw out the closing stages for a third WSL win.

Their unbeaten streak in the WSL, stretching back to October 2025, came to an end with it. The Gunners had not tasted defeat in their last 20 games before their trip to west London.

Victory takes Chelsea to within two points of league leaders Manchester City at the top of the table, while Arsenal are already seven points adrift ahead of their meeting with the champions on October 4.

Image: Alyssa Thompson of Chelsea celebrates her opener with team-mates

Slegers 'disappointed' but believes in her players despite struggles

Arsenal boss Renee Slegers speaking to Sky Sports:

"Very disappointed. We know it's a tough game, Chelsea away. I think we did well in the first half in the physical battle and dominated until their goal. We found it hard in the second half and it cost us more energy.

"[We will] work hard, reflect and go forward. I want to take everything away from the players because I think they're at their very best when they're light. There is so much quality in the squad."

On what isn't clicking for Arsenal currently: "It's a cocktail of things. It's everything. Technical and psychological. We're looking at it. I believe in these players. The goals and the points will come. I believe in them."

On the title race: "We have to earn the right to talk about this because we've lost too many points at the moment. Look at the next game and get the points."

Are Arsenal's title chances over already?

Sky Sports' Dan Long:

It seems a touch early to definitely say whether or not Arsenal's title chances are over already, but their start has left a lot to be desired.

Four games in, they have scored only twice and one of those goals - in the 1-1 draw with Man Utd last weekend - wasn't scored until the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

And now their unbeaten run in the WSL, which started all the way back on October 12 last year, has been ended by Chelsea.

It leaves the Gunners seven points adrift of leaders Man City already.

Head coach Renee Slegers was asked about that topic after full-time at Stamford Bridge and she said she wanted to "take the pressure off" her players.

"I believe in these players. The goals will come and the points will come as well," she said.

"We have to earn the right again to talk about this [the title race] because we've lost too many points."

With a trip to City up next on October 4, the week ahead feels like a crucial one in the north Londoners' season.

Sports.title: Australia suffer ODI series defeat to South Africa
Sports.content:
Australia fell to an ODI series defeat to South Africa with a game to spare as they were beaten by 32 runs in the second ODI match of three in Johannesburg on Sunday.

David Miller (142 off 93 balls) and Temba Bavuma (103 off 116) each smashed centuries for South Africa as they set the visitors a massive 366-run target after being inserted at the toss.

Australia looked well placed early on in their reply, with openers Mitch Marsh (84 off 53) and ​Travis Head (85 off 76) setting the tone by blazing the bowling to all parts.

But ultimately the tourists' middle-order batting issues and struggles against spin were again laid bare. From 191-2 in the 25th over, they added only 62 for the loss of four wickets in the next 15 and a bit overs to stumble to 253-6.

That left Australia needing another 113 runs to win from the final 10 overs and, despite a late counter-punch from Xavier Bartlett (50 off 28), they'd eventually be bowled out for 333 in the final over.

Keshav Maharaj took 2-54, Bjorn Fortuin 2-70 and Aiden Markram 1-55 among the Proteas' spin options. Seamer Lizaad Williams 3-54 and Marco Jansen 2-53.

"It's certainly an area where we need to improve and we're well aware of that," Australia captain ‌Marsh said. "I thought we set up our innings really well in both games but we haven't been able to execute during those middle ‌phases.

"It's a great learning curve, especially for some of our younger players. But you also have to give South Africa full credit for the way they've bowled during those periods."

Miller's eighth ODI ton - containing 12 fours and nine sixes - and captain Bavuma's sixth had helped South Africa to a score of 365-9 from their 50 overs.

Jack Edwards, playing in only his second ODI, grabbed 5-67 and Josh Hazlewood, who dismissed Aiden Markram off the first ball for a golden duck, took 3-70.

Australia, who haven't won a bilateral ODI series against South Africa since 2014, will look for a consolation win in the last game in Potchefstroom on Wednesday. They've lost 19 of their last 25 ODIs against their hosts.

"It was another really good ⁠all-round team performance," Bavuma said. "It started with the bat. ​Conditions were a little tricky up front but we managed to get through ​that period and build towards a good total.

"David played an unbelievable innings and then the bowlers did their job as well."
