View image in fullscreen Harry Kane’s penalty miss was costly for England. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

“Jude likes that, he gets better if that happens,” Tuchel said. “It’s better if he plays with a bit of rage. It’s what he does. I think sometimes he is looking for these moments to get his fire going. He doesn’t know any [Madrid] teammates [during an international game]. He is still friends with them but not for the 90 minutes.”

It was a wild game against Spain. England conceded early and could have been four or five down by the 35th minute. Their defending was loose. They rallied to lead 2-1 at half-time and the match turned after Kane’s penalty miss in the 54th minute when he felt his standing foot give way. Tuchel insisted his team was not far away from beating the very best.

“If Harry doesn’t slip we win the game,” Tuchel said. “If Harry doesn’t slip we go two goals up. We were clearly the better team until that moment. Of course, Spain never panic. How far away are we from that? One small slip from Harry.

“If we had won, we would have deserved it but it wouldn’t have made us favourites for the Euros. We need to go step by step. They came with their strongest team. We had some key players missing. I am fine with this performance. We could have won the game and didn’t.”

Sports.title: James Trafford’s England dream burns with No 1 spot finally up for grabs again
Sports.content:
James Trafford looks genuinely affronted. The Leeds goalkeeper’s reaction borders on incredulity. Was it a season of frustration for him at Manchester City last time out, he is asked? A wasted year? “I won two trophies,” he says very simply and very firmly.

Defiance is the stock in trade of a goalkeeper and Trafford has a nice line in it, on and off the pitch. Thrust into the England lineup against Spain at Wembley on Saturday for only his third cap, he performed well, particularly during the opening 35 minutes when the world champions threatened to run riot. Trafford made two excellent saves that kept England in contention, laying the groundwork for their surge into a 2-1 half-time lead. They ended up losing 3-2 in the Nations League opener after Harry Kane missed a 54th-minute penalty for 3-1.

The question to Trafford was valid because everybody remembers the situation. How he rejoined City, the club of his youth, from Burnley in July last year, ready to be Pep Guardiola’s No 1; the replacement for Ederson, who departed after eight seasons of stellar service. And how, after three Premier League matches, Guardiola went out and signed Gianluigi Donnarumma from Paris Saint-Germain, installing him as his first-choice goalkeeper.

Trafford played in the every round of the Carabao Cup and FA Cup, keeping clean sheets in the finals of both competitions as City beat Arsenal and Chelsea, respectively. “It obviously wasn’t ideal how it panned out but looking back … I got two trophies to my name that I played every game in,” Trafford says. “You take the positives. You play the cards you’re dealt.”

The 23-year-old is looking at a different hand now. It seems as though everything has changed for him since his move to Leeds in August. He has excelled for his new club in their unbeaten start to the Premier League season. No goalkeeper has more saves than his 20 in the competition, nor a higher save percentage than his 85.7%: he has conceded just three times in five games.

Trafford can hear the knock of opportunity with England because, for the first time in eight years, the No 1 position feels up for grabs. Jordan Pickford’s grip on it has been tight since Sir Gareth Southgate turned to him for the 2018 World Cup. Pickford has won 91 caps, keeping 47 clean sheets.

The Everton player has been the undisputed first-choice for so long that there was surprise when Thomas Tuchel started Trafford against Spain and also announced he would play him against Czechia in Prague on Tuesday night. The manager said Pickford would return for the final two matches of this Nations League window – against Croatia in Rijeka and Czechia at Wembley.

View image in fullscreen James Trafford has been in impressive form for Leeds this season. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters

Maybe it was not such a surprise given that Pickford did not totally convince at the World Cup over the summer. He was beaten from distance a few times when it was possible to wonder whether he might have done better. When Enzo Fernández’s shot fizzed past him for Argentina in the semi-final defeat, Jude Bellingham could be seen to exclaim: “It’s [in] the middle of the goal.” The England midfielder was not alone in thinking that.

Pickford let one in at his near post against the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the last 32 and there were too many times when his sorties from his penalty area led to heart flutters among the England supporters. There was the impression that he was sailing close to a grisly error. It must be said that it did not happen.

It is impossible not to read into Tuchel’s decision to share the minutes between Trafford and Pickford – and especially to pitch the former in against Spain. Tuchel said he wanted to see how Trafford handled a high-profile occasion and the answer was: pretty well. Everybody saw and appreciated his one-on-one block from Ferran Torres in the 16th minute. Not everybody noticed the touch he got to Dani Olmo’s low drive on 35 minutes, mainly because the referee did not give a corner.

Trafford is proud of his northern roots; he hails from farming stock in Cumbria. He is down-to-earth, a little unreconstructed. Does he feel his status has changed since his fast start at Leeds? Bah, he wants to say. “It’s all an imaginary thing, status and that,” he says. “It’s how you carry yourself and how you perform.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Has Trafford taken extra confidence into the England camp? “No. Your ability doesn’t change whether you’re playing or not playing. It’s just how you think of it in your head.”

There is nothing imaginary about Trafford’s battle with Pickford, which comes against the backdrop of a dearth of English goalkeepers. With Dean Henderson injured, Tuchel was left to call up Jason Steele as his third-choice. The 36-year-old Brighton goalkeeper has played once for his club this season. He made a total of 10 appearances for them across the previous two campaigns. Who else is there? Aaron Ramsdale has slipped to fourth-choice at Southampton. Nick Pope is not playing at Newcastle. Carl Rushworth has struggled at Coventry this season.

“Me and Picks are both northern lads and we get along really well,” Trafford says. “It’s just the reality in football that everyone competes for the starting XI.”

Trafford is loving life at Leeds and he does accept that playing regularly has made a difference for him with England. “Make no illusions. There are not many players that don’t play that start for any national team.”

And so the dream burns. “It is every goalkeeper’s dream and every footballer’s dream to play for England and start for England,” Trafford says. “Everyone believes they can start. They are just trying to prove that every day.”

Sports.title: Chelsea turn up heat on Arsenal as Alyssa Thompson strike settles WSL derby
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s title chances were dealt a significant blow after a narrow defeat at the hands of Chelsea. Alyssa Thompson’s first-half finish was the difference on a competitive afternoon at Stamford Bridge but one that ultimately left Renée Slegers with more questions than answers about how to save their season.

“Worried? No,” Slegers said. “Confidence is something that fluctuates. They know who they are and they know what they can bring. What’s important is that there’s always phases in the season and there’s different things you need to work on or focus on.

“It’s important that we keep any pressure and any complexity away from the players because we believe in them. It’s just really important that we keep that simplicity and clear minds for the players.”

There is no game quite as eagerly anticipated in the Women’s Super League as the meeting between Chelsea and Arsenal. While other derbies and duels are in their early development, the London derby is the one year after year that brings the pressure, the drama and, of course, the eyeballs. While both sides clearly respect each other off the pitch, there is a distinct sense that once they cross the white line there is true competitive animosity there, one that lifts the levels of everyone in the vicinity.

This edition was no different with expectation and apprehension buzzing around Stamford Bridge before kick-off and no shortage of new narratives. This was the first time Katie McCabe, 11 years a Gunner, would face her old team having moved in the summer. Would she help Chelsea to inflict more pain on Arsenal’s stuttering start, or could Slegers’s side put a pin in the pressure balloon and breathe new life into their search for a first title in eight years?

Both teams came into this encounter having not yet hit form. Arsenal have created opportunities but have looked predictable in their buildup and lacked a finishing touch. In contrast, Chelsea have looked energetic and full of ideas but, excluding their win against Manchester United, have also struggled with ruthlessness in front of goal.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea’s Katie McCabe took on her former Arsenal teammates for the first time since her summer move. Photograph: Harriet Lander/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Sonia Bompastor was handed a significant boost before kick-off with the news that both Keira Walsh and Lauren James were available to start. Lexi Potter was given the nod alongside Walsh in midfield, a sign of how much trust the head coach has in the 20-year-old, while Melvine Malard was fit enough to begin up front.

Slegers, meanwhile, rang the changes from Arsenal’s hard-fought victory against HB Køge during the week. Two who remained were Kyra Cooney-Cross and the goalkeeper Anneke Borbe, who kept out Misa Rodríguez.

The visitors came out full of energy and looking to make an early statement. They dominated early on with 44.2% of the action happening in Chelsea’s defensive third in the first quarter and Arsenal looking to reap the rewards of their high press.

Their biggest threat early on came from Lisa Baum. The 19-year-old has been one of the more positive aspects of their season to date and was given space down the right by Chelsea.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

For all of their control, however, it was much of the same old story for Slegers’s side, haunted by their inability to take their chances. Of the eight shots they created, they failed to register one on target and hit the woodwork twice through Kim Little and Mariona Caldentey.

With every rattle of a post that reverberated around Stamford Bridge, Arsenal’s early confidence dwindled and Bompastor’s side started to find more joy. In direct contrast to their opponents, the Blues took their chance when it came when Malard pounced on Steph Catley as she played out from the back. Borbe made a good save to deny Walsh initially but the rebound fell perfectly for Thompson to hammer home.

It was the ideal time to score and Chelsea went in ahead at the break with the momentum of the game having shifted significantly. They went on to create big opportunities of their own with Malard dragging a shot narrowly wide on two occasions.

While Arsenal were able to create opportunities, the hosts looked comfortable in the circumstances and defended resolutely to see out the game and take home a valuable three points.

Sports.title: Denmark dominate Wales in Nations League as Isaksen adds finishing touch
Sports.content:
Wales wilted in Copenhagen as a 2-0 defeat to Denmark left them bottom of their Nations League group with no points or goals from their first two games.

After a first half in which Wales were very much second-best and fortunate to reach the break level, Denmark’s domination was rewarded by a Ben Davies own goal and a Gustav Isaksen strike in the second period.

Wales lost Thursday’s opener to Portugal 1-0 and Sunday’s result leaves them already facing an uphill battle to avoid relegation from Group A4. Denmark were under similar pressure after being beaten 3-2 by Norway on Thursday, but rose to the occasion and should have won more comfortably.

The Wales manager, Craig Bellamy, had happy memories of the Parken Stadium when as a 19-year-old he had scored the Wales winner in a Euro 2000 qualifier. Bellamy had promised to make changes given the short turnaround of fixtures and, in the event, made six with Charlie Savage’s surprise promotion the most notable switch.

The son of former Wales international Robbie Savage, Charlie joined the squad after several withdrawals, with his previous two caps having both come against Gibraltar. Daniel James, Kieffer Moore and Sorba Thomas formed a reshaped frontline, while Chris Mepham and Connor Roberts were drafted into defence.

View image in fullscreen Craig Bellamy made a number of changes to the team that lost 1-0 in Portugal, but could not deliver a different result. Photograph: Ulrik Pedersen/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

Denmark were soon playing their way through a porous Wales midfield though, and chances came their way. Neco Williams was caught out by Joachim Andersen’s pass from the back and Isaksen flashed his shot wide. Isaksen then sent over a cross that Patrick Dorgu headed off target.

The hosts thought they had taken the lead after 24 minutes. Wales were exposed by a counterattack led by Mikkel Damsgaard and Isaksen met Rasmus Højlund’s cross with a thumping volley, only for VAR to rule offside in the buildup.

Damsgaard struck a post seconds later and it looked a matter of time before Denmark would score. But Dorgu headed off straight down the tunnel in a potential injury blow for Manchester United, and Wales began to create chances of their own.

Thomas was just off target from 20 yards after an Andersen error and Wales went even closer two minutes before the interval. Brennan Johnson got to the byline after working a one-two with Thomas and pulled the ball back to Roberts, whose shot under pressure was tipped away by Filip Jörgensen from close range.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Williams fired straight at Jörgensen at the start of the second half, but Wales were behind after 53 minutes from a free-kick. Damsgaard delivered a delicious ball and, while Højlund wheeled away celebrating the final touch, it ultimately went in off the unfortunate Davies for an own goal.

Isaksen put the contest beyond Wales after 66 minutes. Moore headed off the Wales goalline, but the Lazio winger was quickest on to the loose ball and his deflected strike went in off the underside of the bar.

Mohamed Daramy spurned a great chance to add further Danish gloss and both sides had late efforts ruled out, with Williams’s header disallowed for a push by Ethan Ampadu.

It does not get any easier for Wales with a visit from Erling Haaland’s Norway on Thursday, before a return date against Denmark in Cardiff.

Sports.title: Tony Pulis says he and Stoke were ‘cheated’ in 2011 FA Cup final after Manchester City verdict
Sports.content:
Tony Pulis has said his Stoke City team was “cheated” out of the 2011 FA Cup after Manchester City were found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules.

Pulis’ Stoke lost the 2011 Cup final 1-0 after Yaya Touré’s strike. Yet following Friday’s news that City are guilty on all but one of the more than 100 charges laid by the Premier League in February 2023, Pulis feels serious discontent. City are expected to appeal and they deny any wrongdoing.

“When do we get our FA Cup?” the 68-year-old wrote in his BBC Sport column. “That is what all Stoke fans have been asking me since the news broke on Friday. I thought exactly the same. I don’t expect Manchester City to offer back the 2011 FA Cup and the winners’ medals their players received. I don’t seriously believe any other trophies and titles will be handed back over either. A points deduction and a massive fine feels far more likely.

“But I still feel cheated. We won’t ever get that day back and the chance to celebrate around Stoke-on-Trent with the cup and medals we so honestly fought for. After breaking the rules, Manchester City got to do that instead. While the process is far from over because City are expected to appeal, I have to say this verdict and the whole situation has left a very sour taste in my mouth.”

Pulis pointed to City’s outlay on Touré, who was signed from Barcelona for £24m and earned around £180,000-a-week. He said: “Yaya Touré, who scored the winning goal, was reportedly earning 10 times what we were paying any of our players and, on his own, had cost more than our entire starting 11 when they had signed him from Barcelona in 2010.”

View image in fullscreen Manchester City’s Yaya Touré (left) scores during the 2011 FA Cup final. Photograph: Andrew Yates/AFP/Getty Images

Pulis underlined how his emotion has been changed by the verdict. “My disappointment was buried in the fact we had played a team full of superstars, and faced an elite coach in Roberto Mancini, and had just fallen short. Today, I feel very differently, as I am sure people connected with the other clubs affected by City’s successes in the same period, between 2009 and 2018 [will feel].

“We lost, but to a team that have been found guilty of breaking the financial rules set out by the Premier League. In doing so, they did not just beat Stoke in an FA Cup final, they collected a stack of titles and went on to completely dominate English football for more than a decade. So, with those rules having been broken, what will the punishment be?”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Tony Pulis of Stoke City reacts in defeat. Photograph: Laurence Griffiths/The FA/Getty Images

Pulis believes action may be widespread. “I know all Stoke supporters will be demanding that City pass the trophy over and every club that has been affected by their actions will be considering their legal options,” he said.

On Saturday, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, reiterated the club’s position. “There is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity,” said City’s chair.

On Friday a City spokesperson had said: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023. The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

Sports.title: Liverpool sink Everton and end derby drought after Olsson and Kapocs strike
Sports.content:
At last, their wait is over. Liverpool’s players could gather in front of the Kop for a celebratory team photograph after the final whistle and rejoice in a new feeling, after beating Everton at Anfield in a Women’s Super League fixture for the first time and finally ending their long run of derby pain.

After six wins from six visits to Anfield for Everton in the WSL era and even quips from their former manager Brian Sørensen in previous campaigns about making Anfield their “training pitch” during their persistent run of victories in this showpiece fixture, Beata Olsson’s early header and Cornelia Kapocs’s late finish were enough to give them a deserved 2-0 victory.

“It’s nice to break that duck, definitely,” the Liverpool head coach, Gareth Taylor, said. “We just downplayed the game, if that makes sense, because it becomes something that’s so big that players start to worry. We want players to go out and feel natural, like they’re playing like they were when they were growing up.

“It is nice because it’s a stat that can just grow and grow. I felt we were hard done by [at Anfield] last season – if you look at their xG in that game, they scored four goals but they were absolute worldies, whereas today we’ve scored two [but] we probably could have had six.”

Taylor was not wrong; the hosts were undeniably the better side and should have scored more goals. Indeed, they would have done had it not been for the heroics of the Everton midfielder Ruby Mace.

When Olsson got in front of her marker, Hannah Blundell, to meet Natalia Ramos’s right-sided corner and angle her header perfectly, diagonally across goal and into the far corner inside the first four minutes you could have been forgiven for thinking Liverpool were set for an easy afternoon such was the simplicity of the goal. Instead, what followed was something of a slog at times with Liverpool trying to break down an Everton backline that initially proved difficult to open up.

After the break, another set piece almost did the job for Liverpool but Vivien Endemann’s volley smacked against the crossbar. By now the pressure was almost relentless and, with just over 20 minutes remaining, Ramos looked certain to score, with time to shoot less than 10 yards out. But the effort was blocked by Mace, who threw her body in front of the ball to keep her side in the contest.

Five minutes later, Mace again came to Everton’s rescue and hooked Kapocs’s effort off the line. The Liverpool forward’s attempted header had come off the top of her shoulder and bounced goalwards, but Mace intervened just in time.

View image in fullscreen Cornelia Kapocs fires in Liverpool’s second goal against Everton. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Eventually, Kapocs found room inside the area to turn and fire home in the closing stages, much to the relief of Liverpool’s supporters. The result continued the side’s encouraging start to the campaign as they moved on to seven points from their opening four games, their only defeat having come away against the defending champions, Manchester City.

It took Taylor’s side until 25 January to accumulate seven points last season but they look significantly improved and have built on the progress they made during the second half of 2025-26.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The visitors had spurned a couple of decent chances on the counterattack before the break, including Hannah Cain scuffing over from a promising position. Overall, however, Everton, whose only two league goals this season have been own goals, will be concerned about their comparative lack of creativity.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: Spurs go second, Man Utd earn first win Show Victoria Pelova scored twice as Tottenham moved up to second in the WSL table with a 4-0 win over Aston Villa, while Manchester United earned their first win of the season, edging West Ham 2-1. Dutch midfielder Pelova [pictured] broke the deadlock in the 54th minute at Brisbane Road, and then fired in a second off the underside of the crossbar, taking her tally to four goals in two WSL games. Spurs sealed victory as Caitlin Dijkstra headed in, and Cathinka Tandberg added a fourth with two minutes left. Manchester United secured their first WSL victory under new manager Eva Olid, defeating West Ham in Leigh. Elisabeth Terland’s header set United on their way after nine minutes, with summer signing Andrea Medina doubling the lead late in the second half. Viviane Asseyi scored a late penalty for the visitors. Océane Hurtré fired Birmingham City ahead after 40 seconds against Crystal Palace, scoring the quickest goal of the season so far. Shanade Hopcroft’s long-range free-kick had Palace level on the half-hour, before Hurtré restored Birmingham’s lead with an angled strike. Palace fought back to lead at St Andrew's, their goals coming from Bethany England and Lexi Lloyd-Smith, but Suzu Amano struck with three minutes left to secure Birmingham a point in a thrilling 3-3 draw. Press Assocation Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Asked about that wait for one of his own players to score a league goal, the Everton head coach, Scott Phelan, spoke calmly, saying: “We know we need to be more decisive in those actions, 100%. We have won two games as well and three on the bounce, so we don’t forget that. [But] yes, we want to start contributing more in the final third and that’ll be a challenge for all of us.

“We’ve played four games, so it’s definitely not panic stations. We’ve got good players in those areas of the pitch, we’re convinced they will contribute more – we’ve just got to wait for that moment to appear and hopefully it’s sooner rather than later.”

Phelan’s team still sit comfortably in the middle of the table with two wins from four games. Perhaps the most disappointing aspect for Everton fans will be that they can no longer rely on their annual collection of three points from Anfield.

Sports.title: Messi’s exit leaves Argentina with impossible task of replacing their superhero | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
It isn’t quite over yet. Lionel Messi will return a week on Wednesday for his formal farewell in a friendly against Benin, but, before that, Argentina face two games when they will begin to experience a future without the most potent get-out-of-jail-free card football has known.

Messi’s international career falls into two distinct halves. There was the first decade when there was a sense that he didn’t quite fit, was somehow insufficiently Argentinian, didn’t care for his country. That was always absurd and can be recognised now as a manifestation of the Argentinian public’s frustration at their trophy drought despite the presence in their forward line of one of the best three to play the game.

Then Messi retired, distraught after a missing a penalty in the shootout against Chile in the Copa América final in 2016. Suddenly, Argentina, rather than just lashing out at their biggest star, was forced to confront what it would mean to live without him. The prospect was so appalling it provoked a mass campaign to encourage Messi to reverse his decision.

Since then he has been loved and, despite a shambolic World Cup in 2018, has delivered with two Copas América, a World Cup and another World Cup final. His career was dogged by the accusation that he never matched Diego Maradona’s achievements in a national shirt; he ended up having won more.

This retirement will not be overturned. Messi is 39. Those who persuaded him to change his mind in 2016 were perhaps imagining – hoping for – six more years: they got 10. There will be no second thoughts this time. The rupture is real. No longer when things are going awry will Argentina be able to turn to the superhero in their midst and ask him to fix it.

The best example came almost at the end, when Argentina trailed Egypt 2-0 with 11 minutes of their World Cup last-16 tie remaining. Barcelona youth team coaches used to speak of the teenage Messi “getting the face on”, at which point he would be unstoppable. It happened in Atlanta: it was as though Messi simply decided that wasn’t going to be his last World Cup game. Argentina won without needing extra time.

Optimists will draw solace from the fact that Argentina’s best performance under Lionel Scaloni probably came in their 4-1 victory against Brazil in a World Cup qualifier in March 2025, when Messi did not play. Even allowing for the odd tactical choices of the opposing coach, Dorival Júnior, Argentina were exceptional. Leandro Paredes anchored a midfield as Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernández linked exhilaratingly with Rodrigo De Paul and Thiago Almada on the flanks and Julián Alvarez at centre-forward.

But football is not just about when things are going well. Even in the bleak times, the years of doubt under Edgardo Bauza and Jorge Sampaoli, when games were spiralling out of control, there was always the possibility Messi would put things right. But Argentina now have to deal with a future without that get-out potential.

The post-Messi future begins next week with games against Bolivia and Burkina Faso. Scaloni, has hinted he will sign a contract extension that would take him through to the 2028 Copa América with an option to the 2030 World Cup. That, at least, would provide a measure of stability, but there is little disguising the fact that a new cycle is beginning, just as Scaloni instituted a new era after the 2018 World Cup.

View image in fullscreen Lionel Messi cries at the end of the World Cup final after Argentina’s loss to Spain. Photograph: Stephanie Scarbrough/AP

Other than Messi and Nicolás Otamendi, who are retiring after the Benin valediction, Scaloni named a 35-man squad. Of those, 20 were at the World Cup; given Paredes and Nahuel Molina are serving lengthy bans, that represents a remarkable degree of continuity, although Nicolás Tagliafico, at 34, is also understood to be considering his future. But 12 of the squad had played three internationals or fewer and De Paul and Giovani Lo Celso, who are in their thirties, will play only against Benin, giving the new cohort space to impress in the first two friendlies.

The biggest opportunities, at least in the short term, look to be at the back. Cristian Romero and Lisandro Martínez, both 28, look likely to be the first-choice central defensive pair, but Valentín Gómez of Real Betis and Tomás Palacios, on loan at Estudiantes from Inter, are competing to be back-up.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With Molina suspended, Tagliafico ageing and Gonzalo Montiel injured, the real interest, though, is at full-back, where a pair of 22 year olds could stake a claim to be the future: Agustín Giay of Palmeiras and Román Vega of Zenit.

In Messi’s absence, there remains a question of formation. Although that Brazil game demonstrates what is possible through inter-movement even without a huge amount of overt creativity, it maybe that Scaloni opts for more traditional wingers. Again there are young options: Leonel Flores of Boca Juniors and Roma’s Matias Soulé are likely to make their debuts over the next few days.

And replacing Messi? That’s just not possible, either at a tactical level or, perhaps more significantly, in terms of what he meant for the spirit of the team. It’s not that Argentina need Messi to play well. Indeed, a purist could even argue that Argentina played better in that game that they ever could have played with Messi (or at least the pedestrian Messi of late), because of his lack of movement and the way the game had to be built around him.

That is always the danger with individualists, but Messi was so spectacularly consistent that the percentage option was to rely on his extraordinary genius, the true extraordinariness of which was how reliable it was.

No matter how well-organised an opposition defence, there was also the possibility – the probability even – that he would find an opening, no matter how badly things were going, there was always the chance he would get the face on and sort everything out single-handed.

Plenty of sides have found a new fluency, a more team-based dynamic, after a major star has moved on. Argentina’s ceiling could conceivably rise, but Messi offered a reassurance, a possibility of salvation, that will be sorely missed.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah dropped for Egypt clash as bizarre reason is given for axing
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah dropped for Egypt clash as bizarre reason is given for axing

Mohamed Salah will not feature for Egypt against South Sudan regarding fears over the playing surface.

The Trabzonspor forward has not travelled with the squad for their match at Juba Stadium on Tuesday.

3 Salah has scored 68 goals in 120 caps for Egypt since making his international debut in 2011 Credit: Getty

Salah is not part of the matchday squad for the Africa Cup of Nations qualifier in order to avoid picking up an injury on the astroturf pitch.

The upcoming match in Juba will be played on an artificial surface.

Due to the surface, a decision was made by the Egyptian Football Association (EFA) prior to their previous match for Liverpool legend Salah not to play.

The 34-year-old started Friday's goalless draw against Angola as his side began their qualifying campaign.

However, he will not be part of the side against South Sudan ahead of a potential return for Egypt's friendly clash with South Africa on October 4.

What have the Egypt FA said about Salah?

In a statement, the EFA confirmed their decision as well as explaining the reasoning behind it.

They said: "The Egypt national team's technical staff, led by Hossam Hassan, has decided to rest Mohamed Salah for the match against South Sudan scheduled for 29 September because of the playing surface.

"It was agreed between the national team's technical staff and Mohamed Salah before the Angola match that he would not play against South Sudan, and the technical staff preferred this approach in order to protect the player."

Salah has been captain of the national team since 2019 and has scored 66 goals in 120 caps for his country.

He was also part of their squad at this summer's World Cup, marking his second appearance at the finals.

3 Egypt have decided not to play Salah over fears he will pick up an injury on the astroturf pitch Credit: Getty

Egypt will be hoping he can guide them to a record-extending eighth AFCON title in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda next summer.

However, they have not added to their haul since 2010, with Salah's best finish at the tournament a pair of final defeats in 2017 and 2021.

As well as Angola and South Sudan, the Pharoahs will also face Malawi in their qualifying group.

Salah's absence on Tuesday comes amid a prolific start to his career in Turkey.

The ex-Reds winger joined Trabzonspor in August following his Anfield exit.

He signed a two-year deal with the club after a nine-year spell in the Premier League.

3 Salah started Egypt's goalless draw with Angola on Friday Credit: Getty

Salah has already scored seven goals and added two assists in six league appearances for Trabzonspor.

Those strikes include a hat-trick against Galatasaray in their last outing.

Sports.title: Zinedine Zidane provokes anger from Real Madrid as Kylian Mbappe forced to leave France camp
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe's injury has reportedly created tension between France boss Zinedine Zidane and Real Madrid.

Mbappe linked up with the France squad for the opening round of Nations League fixtures, but was forced off less than an hour into Les Bleus' 1-0 win over Turkey on Friday - five minutes after scoring the decisive goal in Izmit.



2 Mbappe had to be substituted shortly after scoring his 67th international goal Credit: AFP

What injury has Kylian Mbappe picked up?

According to L'Equipe, Real Madrid wanted Mbappe to be rested amid concerns over a knee issue – but Zidane opted to play his captain from the start.

And while scans confirmed Mbappe had not torn his ACL, the 27-year-old has now left the France camp.

It has since been confirmed by Madrid that Mbappe suffered a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left knee.



Zidane is said to have moved the striker into the care of Madrid medical staff quickly in an apparent step to ease tensions.

Madrid boss Jose Mourinho will hope to have his No.10 back as soon as possible, with Los Blancos playing five games between the resumption of the league season after the three-week international break and the end of October.



That run concludes with a trip to Barcelona for the first El Clasico of the campaign.

A blistering start to the season

Mbappe has been in inspired for for Madrid - racking up eight goals in as many games across all competitions at the start of this term.



However, Madrid have endured a rocky start to the new LaLiga season and sit fourth in the table after losing two of their opening seven matches.

They were beaten 2-1 by local rivals Atletico Madrid last time out, going down to ten men early in the second half as Dean Huijsen saw red.

And it proved to be a controversial encounter at the Metropolitano.

2 Mbappe has been involved in all eight of Real Madrid's games so far this season Credit: Getty

Madrid, who were left furious by the referee's decisions, felt Atletico should have had two men sent off themselves.



France's new era up and running

France, meanwhile, minus Mbappe, continue their Nations League League A Group 1 campaign away to Belgium on Monday.

That will be Zidane's second game in charge after he succeeded World Cup-winning manager Didier Deschamps.

Zidane had previously had two spells at the helm of Real Madrid, the club where he spent some of the best years of his playing career.

Between 2016 and 2018, he led them to an incredible three straight Champions League triumphs.



Madrid return to action – with Mbappe available, they'll hope – at home to Villarreal on Saturday, October 10.

Sports.title: Liverpool and Manchester United handed further injury blows as star duo are forced off
Sports.content:
Liverpool and Manchester United handed further injury blows as star duo are forced off

Liverpool and Manchester United's injury woes could be set to intensify after Sunday's Nations League action.

Both Cody Gakpo and Patrick Dorgu were forced off during the first half of their nations' respective matches.

3 Gakpo is the latest Liverpool player to suffer an injury on international duty Credit: Getty

Gakpo was taken off just 17 minutes into the Netherlands' clash with Serbia.

It comes after Alexander Isak left the Sweden camp to return to Merseyside early due to an injury.

The Reds have confirmed the striker will be assessed by the club's medical staff after scoring against Romania on Friday.

How did Cody Gakpo suffer his injury?

Fans will be hoping Gakpo will not be joining Isak on the treatment table in the coming days.

However, they face a nervy wait to discover the severity of the injury which ended his night early against Serbia.

Gakpo was on the end of a strong challenge from Sasa Lukic in the centre of the park just 12 minutes into the match in Belgrade.

Despite initially staying down after the foul, he appeared as if he would be able to continue, only to signal to the bench that he would have to come off moments later.

The 27-year-old was subsequently replaced by Ruben van Bommel in the 17th minute.

It did not appear to affect Xavi's side, though, as they took the lead through a Mexx Meerdink penalty before half-time.

Gakpo has two goals and four assists in six appearances across all competitions so far this season for Liverpool.

3 Gakpo was forced off following a heavy challenge from Lukic during the Netherlands' clash with Serbia Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Andoni Iraola's side return to action at home to Manchester City on Sunday, October 11.

The Reds boss is already without long-term absentees Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike and Conor Bradley.

How did Patrick Dorgu pick up his injury?

As for United, they face similar concerns over Dorgu after he lasted just over half an hour for Denmark against Wales.

The versatile full-back headed straight down the tunnel after limping off in the 31st minute to be replaced by Mohamed Daramy.

Dorgu's injury follows the news that Bruno Fernandes will miss Portugal's match on Sunday.

The Red Devils captain has been ruled out of his country's trip to Norway due to injury.

3 United also now face an anxious wait over the fitness of Dorgu Credit: Getty

Fernandes also missed training on Saturday having been taken off late on against Wales on Thursday.

However, he remains with the squad and has not been ruled out of their final two matches of the international break.

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool striker gets stand named after him at World Cup stadium
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool striker gets stand named after him at World Cup stadium

Celta Vigo have renamed a stand after club legend Iago Aspas ahead of hosting matches at the 2030 World Cup.

The former Liverpool striker will also be honoured with a statue outside the entrance to the stadium.



3 Celta have renamed the Tribuna stand after all-time top scorer Aspas Credit: Getty

Aspas is Celta's all-time leading scorer and appearance maker having returned to his boyhood club for a second spell in 2015.

How many goals has Iago Aspas scored for Celta Vigo?

Either side of a disappointing two years at Anfield, the 39-year-old has scored 223 goals in 578 appearances for the club.

In contrast, the ex-Spain international scored just once in 15 matches for Liverpool between 2013 and 2015.



The veteran forward signed a new one-year deal with Celta in May through to the end of this season.

His legacy has now been immortalised in the stands as well as outside Bailados.



The club are have renamed the Tribuna stand after Aspas as part of their redevelopment project.

Their home since 1928 is currently being expanded ahead of the 2030 World Cup.



Once completed, the capacity will increase from 24,870 to more than 40,000 fans.

Ongoing work on the Gol stand had caused fans to speculate it would be the section named after Aspas.

A total of 7,000 new seats will be installed once it fully reopens in January, with the partially open stand currently holding just 800 supporters.

3 Aspas will also be honoured with a statue outside the entrance to Balaidos Credit: Getty



However, Aspas' name will instead adorn the Tribuna, which has been renamed the Iago Aspas Tribuna.

Mayor of Vigo Abel Caballero confirmed the decision in a video announcement as he responded to the online speculation.

Caballero explained: "Why the Tribuna stand? First, because it is already operational and, therefore, the name is immediate.

"Second, because it will be the stand with the largest capacity in Balaídos.



"And third, very importantly, because next to the Tribuna stand will be the sculpture that the City Council is going to install for Iago Aspas, right there in front."

He added: "Therefore, everything fits. So the Tribuna stand will immediately be called the Iago Aspas Tribuna stand, because it is already operational."

3 Celta's Balaidos will have its capacity increased to more than 40,000 ahead of the 2030 World Cup Credit: Getty

Celta's stadium renovation

Whilst the renovations began last year, work on the Tribuna is not set to begin until later in the season.



The stand will be reconstructed, with its capacity increasing from 5,500 seats to 16,000.

It will also be moved backwards to accommodate the additional seating.

Balaidos has been selected as one of 20 stadiums to be used in Spain, Morocco and Portugal for the 2030 World Cup.

The three nations will co-host the tournament alongside opening matches in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay to mark the World Cup's centenary.



Celta's ground previously hosted matches during the 1982 edition of the tournament, which marks the last time Spain served as hosts.

Sports.title: Calls to strip Man City of Premier League titles as ex-club chairman wants ‘terminal’ punishment
Sports.content:
Manchester City face a 'hammering' after being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules.

That's the view of talkSPORT's Henry Winter, who has also called for Man City to be stripped of the three Premier League titles they won during the period in which they were found to be in breach of the rules.



2 It's been suggested City should be stripped of three Premier League titles, including their first under Pep Guardiola in 2017/18 Credit: Getty

City were found guilty on Friday of the majority of the 115 charges they faced and, if an appeal fails, they could be hit with unprecedented sanctions, including relegation multiple levels down the pyramid.

Asked on talkSPORT by Pete Graves what he thought City's punishment would be, Winter said: "I think they're going to get hammered.

"I think it will be 50 points [deducted] to trigger a relegation [to the Championship] this season, and then we'll see whether [things are taken further].



"There would obviously have to be some sort of agreement with the EFL if they were going to drop them into League One, but as the great [football finance expert] Kieran Maguire points out, that is possible."

Pressed on whether City could even be expelled from the top four divisions altogether and end up in the National League, Winter said: "That is a huge, huge punishment, but the severity of what they've done, as [former City and FA chairman] David Bernstein eloquently pointed out earlier – and he's a Manchester City fan – they absolutely deserve not just to have the whole book thrown at them but almost the whole library."



On the subject of City's Premier League titles from the 2011/12, 2013/14 and 2017/18 seasons, Winter added: "I would wipe those."

The charges cover the period between 2009 and 2018, with Roberto Mancini, Manuel Pellegrini and Pep Guardiola each winning one of those titles.



Earlier, Bernstein had told talkSPORT City needed to be penalised in a way that 'affected their league status'.

"I would first of all say that financial penalties will not be enough," he began. "We're talking about a club with limitless pockets – money doesn't mean very much as we saw in the last transfer window – and whether it's [a fine of] £100m, £200m, that would not be sufficient.

"Unfortunately – I say all of these things with great sorrow, I really do, as a fan – I think there has to be something that will affect their league status.

2 Bernstein was City chairman from 1998 to 2003, overseeing the club's rise back to the top flight Credit: Getty



"And if it was to be a points deduction, it depends on timing. Because if it was today, with the season just a few games in, and the points deduction had to be something that was terminal as far as their Premier League status was concerned, I worked out you'd have to have something like 80 points deducted, which would mean the club could not recover this season and would go down.

"But if this happens at the end of the season, because of the appeals and so on, it's a different kettle of fish, and then you may be talking about an automatic relegation – to which division I don't know.

"I think it does depend partly on the timing."

City continue to protest their innocence over the charges.

Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak reiterated that point in a letter to fans on Saturday, writing: "Following Friday’s media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began."

Meanwhile, talkSPORT understands that City players do not have relegation release clauses in their contracts.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel explains Trent Alexander-Arnold omission for Spain clash as England wait goes on
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel explains Trent Alexander-Arnold omission for Spain clash as England wait goes on

Trent Alexander-Arnold is still waiting to return to the pitch for England.

The Real Madrid right-back was recalled to the squad for the Three Lions' four Nations League games during this international break, but he had to make do with a place on the bench for Saturday's frustrating 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley.



2 Alexander-Arnold hasn't played for England for almost 16 months Credit: Getty

Trent's long wait to add to England caps

Thomas Tuchel opted to start Alexander-Arnold's former Liverpool teammate Jarell Quansah on the right of his back four, and Quansah played the entire game as Alexander-Arnold watched on.

Left out of England's World Cup squad this summer, Alexander-Arnold hasn't featured for his country since a World Cup qualifier against Andorra in June last year.

The 27-year-old is at least in contention to add to his 34 caps to date in England's upcoming matches, though.



The Three Lions continue their Nations League campaign away to Czechia on Tuesday before a trip to Croatia on Saturday.

They then entertain Czechia the following Tuesday as the extra-long international break wraps up.



There ought to be opportunities for Alexander-Arnold given the inevitable need to rotate, but it does seem Quansah is Tuchel's preferred choice at right-back for the time being.

Tuchel praises 'top class' Quansah

Explaining his defensive tactics after the loss to Spain, the England boss said: "We needed Jarell Quansah’s speed and ability to think as a central defender.



"He was top class at the World Cup; he was top class in training this week; he was excellent in this game."

Speaking after bringing Alexander-Arnold back into the fold, Tuchel insisted 'the door is always open' for players to be recalled.

"They had a good start to the season," Tuchel said of Alexander-Arnold and fellow returning star Cole Palmer – who subsequently withdrew from the squad.

2 Tuchel has kept faith with Quansah at right-back after the Bayer Leverkusen player impressed there at the World Cup Credit: Getty



"They never did something wrong. We just chose different players.

"So now it is a new competition. Some players, some positions, have more injuries. Some have less injuries. Cole has his starts that he always had but he has his numbers back – he has his assists back, he has decisive goals back – so that is why he is in the squad.

"I think he has a point to prove, and the same goes for Trent. He was never off the list. He was never non-selectable for us, and it is his chance to show, come to camp and be the best version of himself."

However, Tuchel later called out Palmer for, in his eyes, 'missing too many opportunities' to represent England.

The Chelsea forward also missed the World Cup after a disappointing 2025/26 campaign but has been in superb form early this season.



Manchester United and Republic of Ireland legend Roy Keane also criticised Palmer.

"I like Palmer; he’s a talented boy," he told ITV, "but he’s got far too many bad habits, for me."

Sports.title: Man United handed huge injury scare as star ruled out of international match with ‘complicated problem’
Sports.content:
Man United handed huge injury scare as star ruled out of international match with ‘complicated problem’

Bruno Fernandes has been ruled out of Portugal's match with Norway.

The Manchester United captain started Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales on Thursday night, but was brought off late in the game.

4 Fernandes will sit out Portugal's second of four Nations League games during the international break Credit: Getty



The injury scare has caused him to sit out of training on Saturday.

Portugal manager Jorge Jesus says he will not risk him for the Nations League clash with Norway on Sunday.

“In the game against Wales, we went in with all the available players but Bruno Fernandes came off with a complicated problem,” Jesus said during his press conference.

“We’ll see what happens until tomorrow. Experience tells me that on the third day not all players manage to recover but that’s the same for Norway as for us.

“However, the player who comes in gives as many guarantees as the one who might come off, that’s what I’ll base my decision on.



“The medical team identified these two players as the most concerning, Nuno Mendes could be available for the game.

“The other case [Fernandes] involves treatment and recovery time. He’s coming off an injury at United, and he told me he’s been playing with that pain for the last three games, which is hindering him.



“It was one of the factors that prevented Bruno from playing at his best against Wales.”

Jesus did stress that it was a precautionary measure and it is hoped he can return for next week's game with Denmark.



He added: “I’ve already spoken to him and I prefer not to risk it in this game so he’s fully fit for the Denmark match.”

4 Fernandes has three Premier League goals this season - all in the same game Credit: Getty

Following the Norway match on Sunday, Portugal will face Denmark on October 1 and then Norway again on October 4.

Bruno Fernandes at Man United

Fernandes' three Premier League goals this season all came in the same game when Man United thrashed Ipswich in August.



The United skipper grabbed a hat-trick, and an assist, in the 5-2 victory.

That has proved to be the Red Devils' only league win for Michael Carrick this season.

They have suffered defeats to Hull and Man City, while drawing with Everton and Fulham.

Fernandes did also get on the scoresheet in their 4-0 Champions League victory over Sabah.



4 Fernandes has been United's standout star in recent years Credit: Getty

Bruno Fernandes' future

Fernandes, whose contract is set to expire next summer, has long been linked with a move away from the club with credible interest from Turkey and Saudi Arabia.

talkSPORT's Adrian Durham, however, argued that the Red Devils should have cashed in on him long ago.

He said on talkSPORT's Fiery Fridays: “I know you love Bruno Fernandes and I get it, those numbers were insane in that lazy season he had last season,”



“He can be an absolute bully, usually against poor sides. I get your love for him but just hear me out on this.

“I think Manchester United made a massive error not selling him in the summer [transfer] window.

“You’re probably fuming inside but hold it in for now.

“Bruno Fernandes has just turned 32, so this summer just gone, Bruno’s stock was the highest it could possibly be. Financially, his worth is reducing and reducing.

“His value, according to AI right now, is £35million. His value in the summer – £87m.



4 United will hope Fernandes does not return with more injury problems Credit: Getty

“On what level of business sense does it make sense to keep a player of that age. He’s never going to do those numbers again.

‘So, United should have sold Bruno in the summer. The Player of the Year award would have inflated the fee even more. United could have got a lot of money for him.

“Here’s the thing, we all know they overspent in midfield and underspent in defence.



“They could’ve addressed that situation and I know United fans are thinking we can’t do anything without Bruno, panic without Bruno. We all know this isn’t true.”

He added: “I think this would have made perfect sense, a player right at his peak. He’s only going to fall to age 32 onwards.

“Those numbers aren’t going to come back, this would have made perfect sense. Manchester United have missed a trick, should have sold Bruno in the summer.

Sports.title: Major concern raised about 2/10 England star who is not at same level since Premier League switch
Sports.content:
Major concern raised about 2/10 England star who is not at same level since Premier League switch

Marc Guehi has not been the same player since joining Manchester City.

That's the assessment of talkSPORT's Tony Cascarino on the England centre-back, who was at fault for the opening goal in Saturday's 3-2 Nations League loss to Spain.

2 Guehi was dispossessed by Lamine Yamal with costly consequences Credit: Getty

'England look really short defensively'

Guehi left Crystal Palace for Man City in January and started well under Pep Guardiola but, now with Enzo Maresca in charge, isn't performing 'anywhere near' his previous levels, feels Cascarino.

Speaking on the Weekend Sports Breakfast after England's defeat at Wembley, the former Chelsea and Republic of Ireland striker said: "Defensively, England look really short at the moment. No one stood out in the back line last night.

"I don't think Marc Guehi is playing anywhere near as well as he was a year ago with the performances he put in for Crystal Palace that got him the move to Manchester City.

"Marc Guehi was playing superbly this time last year.

"After initially a good start at City, I don't think he's played to the same level as what he did at Palace.

"If you're looking at small margins, one of the reasons Thomas Tuchel got the job was because they felt like they needed a manager or coach to get them over the line. They've got a team that needs to get over the line."

England on the wrong end of Wembley thriller

England were back in action for the first time since finishing third at this summer's World Cup, where Tuchel drew intense criticism for his tactical approach as the Three Lions blew a 1-0 lead to lose 2-1 to Argentina in the semi-finals.

And Guehi endured a nightmare start to the game against newly crowned world champions Spain.

He was caught in possession on the edge of his own box, allowing Lamine Yamal to pounce and give the visitors the lead inside two minutes.

England came roaring back through goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane to lead at half-time – but after Kane slipped and hit the underside of the crossbar with a penalty, Spain responded courtesy of substitutes Alex Baena, who capitalised on a stray pass from Guehi's City teammate Nico O'Reilly, and Mikel Oyarzabal.

2 Mikel Oyarzabal scored Spain's winning goal against England, just as he did in the Euro 2024 final Credit: Getty

Low marks for Guehi and O'Reilly

And Guehi's difficult night saw him among the three England players who received 2/10 ratings from talkSPORT's Adrian Durham.

Durham asked England legend Stuart Pearce on air whether Guehi and O'Reilly might have been distracted after City were found guilty on Friday of breaching Premier League financial rules.

But Pearce wasn't sure that news played any part in the pair's sub-par displays.

"I wouldn't think so," he replied. "I'll be very, very surprised if that is the case.

"The bottom line is City are so used to dominating the ball, sometimes they've got to check out – recycle it and whatever.

"Tonight there was some good pressing from the Spaniards, and it caught us out."

Sports.title: Ireland stars REFUSE to shake hands of Israeli opponents and bow their heads during national anthem ahead of controversial clash after goalkeeper withdrew from squad in protest at 'atrocities in Gaza'
Sports.content:
Ireland's players bowed their heads during the Israel national anthem and did not shake hands with their opponents before the controversial Nations League clash in Hungary. The fixture has been shrouded in controversy after the Irish team and officials came under huge pressure to stage a boycott due to Israel’s military actions in Gaza. Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad, with the Bolton star saying ‘I am a man of strong faith and try my best to be a person of character and principle’. 'My decision is based purely upon my belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong,' he addded. 'It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition to the Israeli people or the Jewish community but against the atrocities in the region.' Players voted to fulfil the fixture and also agreed to wear black armbands in recognition of all the lives lost in the conflict. Ireland also decided against giving a pennant to Israel to mark the match - a standard gesture in all international fixtures. The customary pre-match handshake did not take place and during the playing of the Israel anthem, Ireland's starting XI looked towards the floor in unison - as did their substitutes. The Ireland XI look to the floor during the playing of the Israel national anthem Israel's players stood for the anthem as Ireland's bowed their heads The Irish side did stand proud for their own national anthem Ireland's substitutes and staff also looked at the floor during Israel's anthem, with the squad having voted to play the match Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad due to Israel's actions in Gaza Heimir Hallgrimsson was heavily criticised in Israel for saying Ireland are 'playing against genocide' Ireland won 3-0 after first-half goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan, who took off his black armband and kissed it when celebrating. There were no handshakes as full time and Ireland’s players were booed as they left the field. Manager Heimir Hallgrimsson had also said that ‘nobody is comfortable playing these games for many reasons’ and, earlier in the week, said his team were ‘playing against genocide’. A training session on Saturday was delayed by five hours after players decided whether to boycott the match which was held in Debrecen, Hungary, with Israel playing in neutral venues due to the conflict. FAI chief executive David Courell said a ‘significant majority’ voted to play. UEFA rules mean teams must name at least three goalkeepers in their squad and Bazunu's withdrawal meant that Jimmy Dunne, the QPR centre back, was named as a keeper on the official team-sheet. Irish broadcaster RTE cut back its screening of the game with no studio punditry, no advertising and only using commentary from an international feed. Many pubs in Ireland refused to show the game and there were protests outside the team hotel in Dublin earlier in the week. Ireland are set to play Israel again on Sunday but it will be behind closed doors at a neutral venue in Serbia.

Sports.title: Former Man City chairman David Bernstein expects club to LOSE Premier League status after being found guilty of vast majority of 115 charges: 'Money won't be enough'
Sports.content:
Manchester City's former chairman David Bernstein believes punishment handed to the club after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules must affect their top flight status. Daily Mail Sport reported that the Premier League has succeeded in proving all of the substantive claims against Man City, with the club found guilty of the 'vast majority' of the 115 charges of financial rule breaking. An appeal from Man City is considered an inevitability, with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak declaring on Saturday that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’. Bernstein, who was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as Football Association chair 2011-13, has warned that financial penalties will not be enough of a punishment. Speaking to talkSPORT, Bernstein stressed the fines would not be sufficient as he cited their vast spending in the previous transfer window. Man City spent £440million in the summer and equalled the British transfer record signing £125million Enzo Fernandez. Man City's former chairman David Bernstein believes the club's Premier League status is at risk after they were found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 rule break charges Bernstein was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as FA chair 2011-13 Bernstein believes that while the club's wealth would render a fine insufficient, Man City could face automatic relegation or a points deduction that effectively ensures they will drop out of the top flight. 'I would first of all say that financial penalties will not be enough,' Bernstein said. 'We're talking about a club with limitless pockets – money doesn't mean very much as we saw in the last transfer window – and whether it's [a fine of] £100m, £200m, that would not be sufficient. 'Unfortunately – I say all of these things with great sorrow, I really do, as a fan – I think there has to be something that will affect their league status. 'And if it was to be a points deduction, it depends on timing. 'Because if it was today, with the season just a few games in, and the points deduction had to be something that was terminal as far as their Premier League status was concerned, I worked out you'd have to have something like 80 points deducted, which would mean the club could not recover this season and would go down. 'But if this happens at the end of the season, because of the appeals and so on, it's a different kettle of fish, and then you may be talking about an automatic relegation – to which division I don't know. 'I think it does depend partly on the timing.' Bernstien suggested Man City's wealth would make a financial penalty for the club 'insufficient' Man City enjoyed staggering success during the years covered by the Premier League charges Man City, who have always strongly denied wrongdoing, were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League with a hearing concluding in December 2024. Their statement that February insisted that they were 'surprised' by the charges. The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period. The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13. They were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023. Between the years mentioned, Manchester City won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League, four FA Cups and seven EFL Cups. Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday that the verdict will trigger a series of legal claims for as much as £800million. In late 2024, Arsenal, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester United served formal notices reserving their right to take action in the event that City – who could now face expulsion from the top flight – be found guilty. Representatives have already begun putting together a case on how much they feel they have a claim for, pointing out that they have lost potential income on the back of City’s cheating. On Saturday, the club hit back in the shape of a strong statement from chairman Al Mubarak, who declared that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’. Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak insisted the club remains confident of clearing their name and ‘proving innocence’ In a lengthy statement, Al Mubarak seemed to make the suggestion that the process had not been fair. He asked fans to study a statement made on Friday by the club closely. That statement read: ‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.' In his message to fans, he wrote: ‘The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began. ‘There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies. ‘While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity.’

Sports.title: Now THAT'S a hydration break! Legends match is stopped so players can drink BEER and a shot in hilarious scenes
Sports.content:
A legends match was halted by a hydration break with a difference, as Real Madrid and Werder Bremen players were presented with a beer and a shot on the pitch. Hydration breaks during the World Cup had largely been booed by fans in stadiums due to matches being delayed as players took on water and received tactical advice from their coaches. The hydration break at Werder Bremen's Weserstadion on Saturday, however, was warmly received. Play was halted in the 32nd minute of the match, which was aimed at marking the 100th anniversary of Werder Bremen's stadium. Servers, who wore white shirts and black aprons, emerged and walked down the touchline carrying trays. A beer and a shot were visible on the trays, which were then presented to the players on the field. Der Traum einiger Fußballer! 🤩😅 Werder Legenden gegen Real Madrid Leyendas live auf Sky Sport Bundesliga, Sky Sport Top Event sowie auf dem Sky YouTube-Kanal! 🍿✅ pic.twitter.com/1G6wBpx9Ya — Sky Sport (@SkySportDE) September 26, 2026 Werder Bremen and Real Madrid legends were presented with a beer and Malteser shot during a hydration break on Saturday Former Werder Bremen star Ailton was seen enjoying a beer on the pitch during the break Brazilian striker Ailton, who helped Werder Bremen win the Bundesliga title back in 2004, was seen picking up and drinking the beer during the break in play. The halting of the match in the 32nd minute was a tribute to former referee Wolf-Dieter Ahlenfelder. Ahlenfelder famously blew the whistle for half-time in the 32nd minute of a match at the stadium between Werder and Hannover back in 1975. The referee, who was persuaded to continue the match, later revealed he had a beer and a Malteser shot at lunch before the game. Ahlenfelder, however, denied being drunk during the match. A beer and Malteser shot reportedly became a popular drink around the stadium following the incident. The legends match featured former Werder Bremen stars Diego, Naldo, Ailton and Per Mertesacker. Claude Makelele, Pepe, Christian Karembeu and Esteban Cambiasso were among those to feature for Real Madrid. Werder Bremen ultimately emerged as 4-3 winners in the match.
